Features

Master doc for feature work added on top of the base RAG pipeline (menu_api.py). Each feature is numbered to match checklist.csv.

Project Roadmap: The Build in Six Phases

Treating AI development with the same engineering rigor as distributed systems — instrumenting every call, benchmarking retrieval quality objectively, and enforcing automated regression barriers — is what turns a brittle proof-of-concept into a resilient, enterprise-ready agent architecture. The build is organized into six phases, each one adding a layer the previous phase didn't have.

Phase 1: Mach 1 (Baseline Proof-of-Concept & Serving)

The foundation centers on proving core retrieval feasibility, establishing vendor-agnostic access, and delivering an interactive interface for early validation.

  • F0 — App Idea & Scope Design: Defining the problem boundary and end-user requirements.
  • F1 — Prototype Execution: Initial validation script testing PDF ingestion and question answering.
  • F2 — Dynamic LLM Selector: Pluggable provider routing (OpenAI, Gemini, Claude, Ollama) to eliminate vendor lock-in.
  • F3 — Semantic RAG & Vector Store: Chunking pipeline and dense indexing using FAISS.
  • F3.1 — RAG System Prompt & Persona: Enforcing role boundaries, response formatting, and grounding guardrails.
  • F4 — FastAPI Asynchronous Backend: Exposing the retrieval pipeline over a standardized REST API with streaming support.
  • F5 — Interactive Web Interfaces: Web-based browser playgrounds powered by Streamlit and Gradio.

Phase 2: Bullitt (Observability, Context & Data Foundation)

Once the baseline pipeline operates, the focus shifts toward runtime visibility, context refinement, and structured tool integration.

  • F6 — Token & Cost Accounting: In-code telemetry tracking prompt/completion tokens and dollar costs per invocation. (Blog article: In-Code Token & Cost Accounting - F6)
  • F7 — Conversational Memory Buffering: Short-term conversational context layers for multi-turn disambiguation. (Blog article: Ephemeral Chat Memory - F7)
  • F9 — Distributed Tracing: End-to-end latency profiling and error tracking across the retriever and LLM steps. (Blog article: Observability & Tracing - F9)
  • F10 — FlashRank Cross-Encoder Re-ranking: Two-stage retrieval using models like FlashRank to maximize chunk density and precision. (Blog article: Cross-Encoder Re-ranking - F10)
  • F11 — Deterministic Text-to-SQL Engine: Queryable SQLite integration (usage_log) for deterministic arithmetic and historical aggregations. (Blog article: Relational DB & Text-to-SQL Tool - F11)
  • F8 — FastMCP Server Integration: Exposing backend operational data (such as live Google Sheets for daily specials and holiday hours) via the Model Context Protocol. (Blog article: FastMCP Server Endpoint - F8)

Phase 3: Fox Body (Multi-Engine & Agent Frameworks)

This layer introduces protocol interoperability and modular multi-agent architectures, separating execution strategies behind clean interfaces.

  • F12 — Strategy Factory Pattern: A shared base interface allowing seamless runtime switching between execution engines. (Blog article: Modular Engine Strategy Factory: One Fixed Chain Isn't Enough Anymore: Building the Plug Before the Appliances - F12)
  • F12.1 — Parallel Entry Point: A backward-compatible second entry point built on the same factory, proving the multi-engine architecture via the Strangler Fig pattern without touching the original API.
  • F13 — LangGraph StateGraph Engine: Graph-based cyclical reasoning, conditional branching, and retry logic. (Blog article: LangGraph - F13)
  • F14 — CrewAI Multi-Agent Coordination: Collaborative task delegation between specialized role-based personas.
  • F15 — AutoGen Collaborative Swarm: Conversational consensus loops between user proxy and assistant agents.

Phase 4: Coyote 5.0 (Resilience, Evals & Hybrid Retrieval)

Scaling production workloads requires durable session storage, hybrid search recall, and objective quality benchmarking.

  • F16 — SQLite Persistent Checkpointing: Disk-backed state persistence so a session survives a server restart. (Blog article: Persistent Thread Checkpointing: Chat History: Surviving Server Restarts with SQLite - F16)
  • F17 — Automated RAG Evaluation Suite: Quantitative scoring of faithfulness, answer relevance, and context precision via LLM-as-judge, run against every cuisine's real menu. (Blog article: Automated RAG Evals Harness: Turning "Did That Change Help or Hurt?" Into a Number - F17)
  • F18 — Hybrid Search Fusion (BM25 + FAISS): Blending sparse keyword matching with dense semantic search for maximum retrieval recall.

Phase 5: Dark Horse (Enterprise Production Hardening)

With the multi-engine and resilience layers in place, this phase moves from "does it work" to "can it be trusted" — gating what questions get answered and what changes get shipped.

  • F19 — Query Guardrails & Intent Gating: A Pydantic-structured classifier that labels each question's intent up front, replacing ad hoc keyword routing with consistent, measurable off-topic rejection.
  • F20 — CI/CD Eval Regression Gate: Automated GitHub Actions workflow executing Automated RAG Evaluation Suite (F17) on every pull request to block merges if accuracy or faithfulness regresses. Done — see F20's full write-up below. (Blog article: CI/CD Eval Regression Gate: Turning F17's Eval Suite From 'Available' Into 'Enforced' - F20)

Phase 6: Shelby Cobra (Security & Quality Hardening)

The final milestone locks down the perimeter and the core logic itself — authenticating requests, screening adversarial input, and proving the supporting code holds up under test, independent of any LLM call.

  • F21 — API Authentication & Rate Limiting: Request-layer authentication and throttling to block unauthorized access and abuse before it reaches the pipeline.
  • F22 — Prompt-Injection Defense: Delimiter-based isolation and pattern filtering that treats retrieved content as data, not instructions, blocking commands hidden inside a menu PDF or a sheet row.
  • F23 — Unit Tests for Core Modules: A pytest suite covering the database, sheets, and re-ranking modules in isolation — every external dependency (Google Sheets, the cross-encoder model, disk) mocked at the boundary, so the logic is proven independent of any LLM call. Done — see F23's full write-up below. (Blog article: Unit Tests for Core Modules: Testing the Logic, Not the Vibes - F23)
Status note: bold items above are actually built and verified — Phases 1 and 2 (F0–F11) in full, plus F12/F12.1, F13, F16, F17, F20, and F23. The unbolded items (F14, F15, F18, F19, F21, F22) are detailed, planned write-ups — architecture and intent decided, not yet implemented — same distinction the individual F-sections below make in their own Status lines.

Suites

Basic Suite AI/LLM, RAG

Pros:

  • Fast time-to-value — a working, cited RAG chatbot over your own data, no agent complexity to build or debug.
  • Minimal moving parts — one fixed chain, easy to reason about, cheap to run (single LLM call per turn).
  • Solid foundation — nothing here gets thrown away; the Enterprise Agentic Suite is built directly on top of it.

How it covers the 5 areas:

  • Prompt Engineering — ✅ F3.1
  • Context Engineering — partial: F3 only
  • Agent/Harness Design — not included
  • Evals — not included (manual testing only, via F2/F4/F5)
  • Observability & Production Hardening — not included

Enterprise Agentic Suite AI/LLM, RAG, Agentic

Pros:

  • Everything in Basic Suite, plus memory, tool use, multi-engine orchestration, and self-correction.
  • Automated evals gate every change — regressions caught in CI, not by an unhappy customer.
  • Production-grade — authentication, rate limiting, and prompt-injection defense built in.
  • Full observability — every call is cost-tracked and traced.

How it covers the 5 areas (full coverage):

  • Prompt Engineering — ✅ inherits F3.1
  • Context Engineering — ✅ F6, F7, F10, F16, F18
  • Agent/Harness Design — ✅ F8, F12, F12.1, F13, F14, F15, F19
  • Evals — ✅ F17, F20, F23
  • Observability & Production Hardening — ✅ F9, F11, F21, F22

3 Agentic engine types to choose from (pick one via F12's strategy factory):

  • LangGraph State Machine (F13) — a single agent following an explicit graph that checks and retries its own work. Most predictable and cheapest to run; best when you need deterministic, auditable step-by-step control flow.
  • CrewAI Multi-Role (F14) — splits the work across specialized roles (e.g. a "menu expert" + a "policy expert") that each own one slice of the answer, then merges them. Best when a question spans multiple domains of expertise.
  • AutoGen Multi-Agent (F15) — two agents converse — one proposes, one critiques — iterating until they agree. Best for accuracy-critical answers, catching mistakes a single pass would miss, at the cost of more rounds and tokens.

Getting Started

1) Install requirements & set up .env

python3 -m venv venv                  # skip if venv/ already exists
source venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements.txt

Then create a .env file at the repo root (alongside this features.html and requirements.txt) with one of the following:

# OpenAI
OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-...

# or Azure OpenAI
AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY=...

The app checks for OPENAI_API_KEY first, then falls back to AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY — it exits with an error at startup if neither is set. This is also where DEBUG_MODE gets set later (step 6 below).

2) Run with Python (CLI, no server)

source venv/bin/activate
python3 menu_api.py

Builds/loads the FAISS vectorstores, then prompts you to pick a cuisine (sushi/steak/italian) and drops into an interactive Q&A loop (q to quit). Good for a quick check, but this path never hits the /ask endpoint.

3) Run with uvicorn (FastAPI server)

source venv/bin/activate
uvicorn menu_api:app --reload --port 8000

Leave this running in its own terminal — it's required before testing via curl/Postman/Streamlit/Gradio, since all of them send HTTP requests to http://127.0.0.1:8000.

4) Test in Streamlit

source venv/bin/activate
streamlit run web-demo/streamlit_app.py

Requires the uvicorn server above to already be running. Opens a browser UI to pick a cuisine and ask questions against the /ask endpoint.

5) Test in Gradio

source venv/bin/activate
python3 web-demo/gradio_app.py

Also requires the uvicorn server above to already be running. Launches a Gradio UI in the browser, same idea as Streamlit, hitting the same /ask endpoint.

6) Set DEBUG_MODE

Env var, read via os.environ.get("DEBUG_MODE", "true") in menu_api.py — defaults to on if not set at all. To turn it off, add this line to the .env file at the repo root (same file that holds OPENAI_API_KEY):

DEBUG_MODE=false

Restart whichever process you're running (uvicorn or python3 menu_api.py) for the change to take effect — it's only read once, at import time. See the DEBUG_MODE section below for exactly what this silences.

↑ Back to top

DEBUG_MODE & METRICS — debug/testing toggles

Two related env vars, deliberately split apart so tracking/persistence never silently stops just because console noise gets turned off.

METRICS — read via os.environ.get("METRICS", "true"), defaults to on. Controls whether In-Code Token & Cost Accounting (F6)'s token/cost tracking, Observability & Tracing (F9)'s latency capture, and Relational DB & Text-to-SQL Tool (F11)'s log_call persistence happen at all. Set METRICS=false to skip all of it — no DB writes, no usage/ session_totals fields in the /ask response.

DEBUG_MODE — read via os.environ.get("DEBUG_MODE", "true"), defaults to on. Set DEBUG_MODE=false in .env (or the shell env) to silence diagnostic console output:

  • the Using provider: ... line and the startup LLM connectivity test (Test prompt response: ...)
  • the CLI's chunk stats (Total chunks: ..., Average chunk size: ...)
  • the [F8] Accessing MCP data source... notice
  • the F13 CLI prompt to override DEFAULT_ENGINE per run
  • the [F6]/[F9]/[F11] console print lines — but only when METRICS is also on; DEBUG_MODE no longer decides whether tracking happens, only whether it prints

Originally DEBUG_MODE alone gated both the tracking and the printing for F6/F9/F11. That meant setting DEBUG_MODE=false for a quieter run also silently stopped Relational DB & Text-to-SQL Tool (F11)'s durable cost records from being written at all — a real gap for a feature whose entire point was surviving past the in-memory session. METRICS was split out to fix that: tracking/persistence now runs whenever METRICS is on (the default), and DEBUG_MODE only controls whether that activity is also printed to the console.

Why this exists, in plain English: before spending time on a web server, a database, or a UI, you want to answer one question as cheaply as possible: does the core idea even work? Can an LLM correctly answer questions about a restaurant's menu if you just hand it the PDF? Building that as a single, throwaway script — no API framework, no auth, no error handling for edge cases — is the fastest way to find out. Everything else in this project (the FastAPI server, the web UIs, the cost tracking, the live Google Sheet integration) only exists because this first, rough version proved the underlying approach was sound.

Maps to checklist.csv day 1, "Prototype" — the first working version of the RAG pipeline, built as a notebook before it became menu_api.py.

Where: prototype/Demo_01_Building_a_RAG_Powered_FAQ_Agent_with_Custom_Knowledge.ipynb — the original notebook. Later cleaned up into a standalone menu_rag.py script (and back into a matching menu_rag.ipynb), per project-notes.txt's ADDITIONAL FEATURES section.

What it does:

  • proves out the RAG pipeline end-to-end in one file: load a menu PDF, split it into chunks, embed the chunks into a FAISS vectorstore, build a RetrievalQA chain, and run a sample query
  • menu_rag.py/menu_rag.ipynb are the standalone descendants of this same pipeline — still runnable independently of menu_api.py, just without the FastAPI/web-UI layers added later (F4/F5)

How to run:

source venv/bin/activate
python3 menu_rag.py

Or open prototype/Demo_01_...ipynb or menu_rag.ipynb in VS Code/Cursor (Jupyter + Python extensions), select this folder's venv as the kernel, and run all cells. Either way you get the same chunk-metrics print, sample query, and interactive question loop menu_api.py's CLI mode (F2/F3) later inherited.

#!/usr/bin/env python
# coding: utf-8

# # Demo: Building a RAG-powered FAQ Agent with Custom Knowledge

# Step 1: Install required packages -> see requirements.txt

# Step 2: Import dependencies
import os
from dotenv import load_dotenv, find_dotenv
from langchain_openai import (
    AzureChatOpenAI,
    AzureOpenAIEmbeddings,
    ChatOpenAI,
    OpenAIEmbeddings,
)
from langchain_community.document_loaders import PyPDFLoader
from langchain_text_splitters import RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter
from langchain_community.vectorstores import FAISS
from langchain_classic.chains import RetrievalQA

# Step 3: Set credentials (loaded from shared .env at the repo root, OpenAI or Azure)
load_dotenv(find_dotenv())

if os.environ.get("OPENAI_API_KEY"):
    provider = "openai"
    llm = ChatOpenAI(model="gpt-4o-mini", temperature=0)
    embeddings = OpenAIEmbeddings(model="text-embedding-3-small")
elif os.environ.get("AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY"):
    provider = "azure"
    llm = AzureChatOpenAI(
        azure_endpoint="https://openai-api-management-gw.azure-api.net",
        api_version="2025-01-01-preview",
        deployment_name="gpt-5-mini",
    )
    embeddings = AzureOpenAIEmbeddings(
        azure_endpoint="https://openai-api-management-gw.azure-api.net",
        api_version="2023-05-15",
        deployment="text-embedding-ada-002",
    )
else:
    raise RuntimeError("Set OPENAI_API_KEY or AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY in the .env file")

print(f"Using provider: {provider}")

# Quick connectivity test — a plain prompt, no FAQ document needed
test_response = llm.invoke("Say 'connection ok' if you can read this.")
print("Test prompt response:", test_response.content)

# Full RAG pipeline — hardcoded to the sushi menu for now

# Load and chunk PDFs using PyPDFLoader and RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter
available_cuisines = ["sushi", "steak", "italian"]
cuisine = input(f"Which menu would you like ({'/'.join(available_cuisines)})? ").strip().lower()
while cuisine not in available_cuisines:
    cuisine = input(f"Please choose one of {'/'.join(available_cuisines)}: ").strip().lower()
menu = f"menus/{cuisine}.pdf"

# 2.1 Load and chunk PDFs using PyPDFLoader 
loader = PyPDFLoader(menu)
documents = loader.load()

# 2.2 Load and chunk PDFs using RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter
text_splitter = RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter(chunk_size=500, chunk_overlap=50)
docs = text_splitter.split_documents(documents)

# 2.3 Generate embeddings (OpenAI or Azure OpenAI, per provider above) and store in FAISS vectorstore
vectorstore = FAISS.from_documents(docs, embeddings)

# 2.4 Run retrieval queries with GPT to fetch contextually relevant chunks
qa_chain = RetrievalQA.from_chain_type(
    llm=llm,
    retriever=vectorstore.as_retriever(),
    return_source_documents=True,
)

# 3.1 Analyze the chunking results: total chunk count and average chunk size
chunk_sizes = [len(doc.page_content) for doc in docs]
print(f"\nTotal chunks: {len(docs)}")
print(f"Average chunk size: {sum(chunk_sizes) / len(chunk_sizes):.0f} characters")

# 3.2Sample query and top matching result
query = "What sushi rolls are on the menu?"
result = qa_chain.invoke({"query": query})

print("\nAnswer:", result["result"])
# print("\n--- Top matching result ---")
# print(result["source_documents"][0].page_content)

# print("\n--- All sources ---")
# for i, doc in enumerate(result["source_documents"], 1):
#     print(f"\nSource {i}:")
#     print(doc.page_content)

# 3.3 Ask the user a question and get the answer from the RAG chain (loop until 'q' to quit)
while True:
    user_query = input(f"\nWhat would you like to know about the {cuisine} menu? (q to quit) ")
    if user_query.strip().lower() == "q":
        break
    user_result = qa_chain.invoke({"query": user_query})
    print("\nAnswer:", user_result["result"])

Line-by-Line Deep Dive

L9-20 imports
os/dotenv for credentials; the four langchain_openai classes give both a chat model and an embeddings model for each provider (OpenAI vs. Azure) — the chat model answers questions, the embeddings model turns text into vectors for similarity search, and they're separate objects because they're separate API calls under the hood. PyPDFLoader reads the PDF, RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter chunks it, FAISS is the vector index, RetrievalQA is the pre-built LangChain chain that glues retrieval + generation together.
L23 load_dotenv(find_dotenv())
find_dotenv() walks up parent directories looking for a .env file instead of assuming a fixed relative path — this is what lets every script in this project (this one, menu_api.py, etc.) share one .env at the repo root without each needing to know its own depth in the folder tree.
L25-42 provider selection
Checks for OPENAI_API_KEY first, falls back to AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY, and raises RuntimeError immediately if neither is set. Why raise instead of defaulting to something: failing loudly at import time, before any PDF is touched, means a misconfigured environment is caught in under a second — not after the user has already waited for chunking and embedding to run.
L44-48 connectivity smoke test
One throwaway llm.invoke(...) call before doing any real work. This is deliberately wasteful (it costs a fraction of a cent) in exchange for certainty: if the API key is wrong or the network is down, you find out in one second instead of after the PDF has already been loaded, split, and embedded.
L53-56 cuisine input loop
A while loop that re-prompts until the input matches available_cuisines exactly — the simplest possible input guard, appropriate for a script only the developer runs by hand.
L60-61 PyPDFLoader(menu).load()
Returns one LangChain Document per PDF page, each with the page's raw extracted text in .page_content. No chunking happens here yet — a full page is still one document at this point.
L64-65 RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter(chunk_size=500, chunk_overlap=50)
Splits each page into ~500-character chunks with 50 characters of overlap between consecutive chunks. Why overlap: without it, a sentence that straddles a chunk boundary gets cut in half in both resulting chunks, and neither half alone may contain enough context to answer a question about it.
L68 FAISS.from_documents(docs, embeddings)
Embeds every chunk (one API call per chunk, batched) and builds an in-memory similarity index over the resulting vectors. Interview-relevant gap: this recomputes embeddings from scratch on every run — there's no caching. That's exactly the gap menu_api.py's build_qa_chain() closes later (F4) with index_path/FAISS.load_local.
L71-75 RetrievalQA.from_chain_type(...)
return_source_documents=True is the one non-default argument — without it, the chain would only return the generated answer text, with no way to show which chunk it was actually grounded in. That source-document transparency becomes the top_match field the API (F4) later exposes.
L78-80 chunk stats
A quick sanity print — total chunk count and average chunk size — to eyeball whether the splitter settings are behaving reasonably before trusting the retrieval step downstream.
L96-101 interactive loop
A bare while True REPL: read a question, invoke the chain, print the answer, repeat until q. No conversation memory between turns (each invoke is independent) — that gap is what Ephemeral Chat Memory (F7) fixes later.
Interview angle — "Why start with a script instead of the API?" This is a spike: the goal was to de-risk the one unproven assumption (retrieval-augmented generation actually working well against this menu data) as fast as possible, with zero incidental complexity — no HTTP framework, no request/response models, no auth. Everything a web layer adds (FastAPI in F4) is orthogonal to whether the RAG approach itself is sound, so it's deliberately deferred until after that question is answered.

Why this exists, in plain English: this app can run on two different AI providers — OpenAI directly, or Azure's hosted version of OpenAI — depending on which API key is available. Picking the wrong one, or having a bad/expired key, is one of the most common setup mistakes. Instead of letting that failure surface confusingly later (in the middle of building a search index, or worse, on a customer's first real question), the app checks "am I even talking to the right AI, and is it actually responding?" the moment it starts up.

Maps to checklist.csv day 2, "LLM Selector" — this is the diagnostic check that confirms the selected provider is actually reachable before the app does any real work.

Where: near the top of menu_api.py, right after the provider is chosen (OpenAI vs. Azure OpenAI) — runs once at import time, so it fires whether the module is loaded by uvicorn or by python3 menu_api.py directly.

What it does (gated by if DEBUG_MODE:):

  • prints Using provider: openai (or azure) so you can confirm which credentials got picked up
  • sends one throwaway prompt — llm.invoke("Say 'connection ok' if you can read this.") — and prints the reply as Test prompt response: ..., confirming the API key/endpoint actually works before you try to use the RAG chain

How to test:

source venv/bin/activate
uvicorn menu_api:app --reload --port 8000

Watch the terminal at startup — you'll see the provider line and the connectivity test response before the "Application startup complete" log. Same output appears if you run python3 menu_api.py instead. Set DEBUG_MODE=false in .env and restart to confirm both lines disappear.

#!/usr/bin/env python
# coding: utf-8

# # Demo: Building a RAG-powered FAQ Agent with Custom Knowledge

# Step 1: Install required packages -> see requirements.txt

# Step 2: Import dependencies
import os
from dotenv import load_dotenv, find_dotenv
from langchain_openai import (
    AzureChatOpenAI,
    AzureOpenAIEmbeddings,
    ChatOpenAI,
    OpenAIEmbeddings,
)
from langchain_community.document_loaders import PyPDFLoader
from langchain_text_splitters import RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter
from langchain_community.vectorstores import FAISS
from langchain_classic.chains import RetrievalQA
from langchain_core.prompts import ChatPromptTemplate
from langchain_core.prompts.chat import SystemMessagePromptTemplate, HumanMessagePromptTemplate
from typing import Optional
from fastapi import FastAPI
from pydantic import BaseModel
from core.telemetry import UsageInfo, new_session_totals, track_usage, new_trace_totals, trace_call, log_trace  # F6, F9
from core.memory import wrap_with_memory  # F7
from core.vectorstore import wrap_with_reranking  # F10
from core.database import init_db, log_call, get_session_totals  # F11
from core.sheets import get_daily_specials, get_hours_and_events, detect_ops_intent, resolve_target_days  # F8

# Step 3: Set credentials (loaded from shared .env at the repo root, OpenAI or Azure)
load_dotenv(find_dotenv())

# F2/F3/F6: general debug/testing toggle - set DEBUG_MODE=false in .env to silence
# provider info + connectivity test (F2), chunk stats (F3), and usage/cost tracking (F6)
DEBUG_MODE = os.environ.get("DEBUG_MODE", "true").lower() != "false"

if os.environ.get("OPENAI_API_KEY"):
    provider = "openai"
    llm = ChatOpenAI(model="gpt-4o-mini", temperature=0)
    embeddings = OpenAIEmbeddings(model="text-embedding-3-small")
elif os.environ.get("AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY"):
    provider = "azure"
    llm = AzureChatOpenAI(
        azure_endpoint="https://openai-api-management-gw.azure-api.net",
        api_version="2025-01-01-preview",
        deployment_name="gpt-5-mini",
    )
    embeddings = AzureOpenAIEmbeddings(
        azure_endpoint="https://openai-api-management-gw.azure-api.net",
        api_version="2023-05-15",
        deployment="text-embedding-ada-002",
    )
else:
    raise RuntimeError("Set OPENAI_API_KEY or AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY in the .env file")

if DEBUG_MODE:  # F2: test the LLM - print provider + run a connectivity check
    print(f"Using provider: {provider}")

    # Quick connectivity test — a plain prompt, no FAQ document needed
    test_response = llm.invoke("Say 'connection ok' if you can read this.")
    print("Test prompt response:", test_response.content)

# Full RAG pipeline, wrapped as a reusable function (built once per cuisine, cached by the API below)

# Vectorstore directory
VECTORSTORE_DIR = "vectorstores"

# System prompt for the RAG chain - replaces RetrievalQA's generic default (a bare "use this
# context, say I don't know" instruction) with a consistent restaurant-assistant persona, an
# explicit no-hallucination guardrail, and date-context awareness (matters now that F8 feeds
# this chain resolved dates for hours questions - see with_date_context() below).
RAG_SYSTEM_PROMPT = """You are a friendly, knowledgeable restaurant assistant. Answer guest questions
using ONLY the menu and restaurant information given in the context below - never
invent dishes, prices, ingredients, allergens, or policies that aren't explicitly
there.

Guidelines:
- If the answer isn't in the provided context, say so plainly (e.g. "I don't have
  that information") rather than guessing.
- If the question references a specific date or day (e.g. "today", "Friday",
  "this weekend"), use that to figure out which part of the context applies.
- Keep answers concise and conversational, like speaking to a guest at the
  restaurant - not a bulleted data dump unless they asked for a list.
- Mention prices when referencing specific dishes, if the context gives them.
- If asked about something outside the menu or restaurant policies, politely
  redirect back to what you can help with instead of answering off-topic.
----------------
{context}"""

RAG_PROMPT = ChatPromptTemplate.from_messages([
    SystemMessagePromptTemplate.from_template(RAG_SYSTEM_PROMPT),
    HumanMessagePromptTemplate.from_template("{question}"),
])


def build_qa_chain(cuisine: str):
    menu = f"menus/{cuisine}.pdf"
    # Index path for the vectorstore
    index_path = f"{VECTORSTORE_DIR}/{cuisine}"

    # 2.1 Load and chunk PDFs using PyPDFLoader
    loader = PyPDFLoader(menu)
    documents = loader.load()

    # 2.2 Load and chunk PDFs using RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter
    text_splitter = RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter(chunk_size=500, chunk_overlap=50)
    docs = text_splitter.split_documents(documents)

    # 2.3 Generate embeddings (OpenAI or Azure OpenAI, per provider above) and store in FAISS vectorstore,
    # or load a previously saved index from disk to avoid re-embedding every run
    if os.path.exists(index_path):
        vectorstore = FAISS.load_local(index_path, embeddings, allow_dangerous_deserialization=True)
    else:
        vectorstore = FAISS.from_documents(docs, embeddings)
        vectorstore.save_local(index_path)

    # 2.4 Run retrieval queries with GPT to fetch contextually relevant chunks
    retriever = wrap_with_reranking(vectorstore.as_retriever())  # F10: cross-encoder re-ranks the retrieved chunks
    qa_chain = RetrievalQA.from_chain_type(
        llm=llm,
        retriever=retriever,
        return_source_documents=True,
        chain_type_kwargs={"prompt": RAG_PROMPT},
    )
    return qa_chain, docs


available_cuisines = ["sushi", "steak", "italian"]

qa_chains = {}
docs_by_cuisine = {}
for c in available_cuisines:
    qa_chains[c], docs_by_cuisine[c] = build_qa_chain(c)

qa_chains_with_memory = {}  # F7
for c in available_cuisines:
    qa_chains_with_memory[c] = wrap_with_memory(lambda q, chain=qa_chains[c]: chain.invoke({"query": q}))

app = FastAPI()

session_usage_totals = new_session_totals()  # F6
session_trace_totals = new_trace_totals()  # F9
init_db()  # F11: create usage_log table if it doesn't exist yet

class AskRequest(BaseModel):
    cuisine: str
    question: str
    session_id: str = "default"  # F7

def format_specials_answer(rows: list[dict]) -> str:  # F8: shared by /ask and the CLI
    if not rows:
        return "There are no active specials for that day."
    lines = [f"[{row['Day']}] {row['Dish Name']} ({row['Price']}) - {row['Description']}" for row in rows]
    return "Specials:\n" + "\n".join(lines)

def format_hours_events(rows: list[dict]) -> str:  # F8: shared by /ask and the CLI - "" when there's nothing to append
    if not rows:
        return ""
    lines = [
        f"{row['Date']} ({row['Day']}) - {row['Event / Holiday']}: {row['Status']} "
        f"{row['Open Time']}-{row['Close Time']}"
        for row in rows
    ]
    return "\n\nGoogle Sheets (F8) - holiday/event schedule for that day:\n" + "\n".join(lines)

def specials_for_question(question: str) -> list[dict]:  # F8: resolves tomorrow/weekend/a weekday/etc., dedupes "All Week" rows
    rows, seen = [], set()
    for d in resolve_target_days(question):
        for row in get_daily_specials(d.strftime("%a")):
            if row["Dish Name"] not in seen:
                seen.add(row["Dish Name"])
                rows.append(row)
    return rows

def hours_for_question(question: str) -> list[dict]:  # F8: resolves tomorrow/weekend/a weekday/etc.
    rows = []
    for d in resolve_target_days(question):
        rows.extend(get_hours_and_events(d.isoformat()))
    return rows

def with_date_context(question: str) -> str:  # F8: shared by /ask and the CLI
    # The RAG chain has no way to resolve "today"/"tomorrow"/"this weekend" on its own -
    # the PDF's hours section is a static weekly schedule, so relative-day phrasing fails
    # to resolve without this, even though the schedule itself is in the retrieved chunk.
    target_days = resolve_target_days(question)
    if len(target_days) == 1:
        d = target_days[0]
        prefix = f"The date being asked about is {d.strftime('%A')}, {d.isoformat()}. "
    else:
        parts = ", ".join(f"{d.strftime('%A')} {d.isoformat()}" for d in target_days)
        prefix = f"The dates being asked about are: {parts}. "
    return prefix + question

@app.post("/ask")
def ask(request: AskRequest):
    cuisine = request.cuisine.strip().lower()
    if cuisine not in qa_chains:
        return {"error": f"Unknown cuisine. Choose one of {available_cuisines}"}

    if request.question.strip().lower() == "tt":  # F11: totals-only shortcut, works regardless of DEBUG_MODE
        return {"cuisine": cuisine, "session_totals": get_session_totals(request.session_id)}

    ops_intent = detect_ops_intent(request.question)  # F8: route obvious specials/hours questions to the live sheet
    if ops_intent == "specials":  # F8: specials only ever live in the sheet, never in the PDF menus - go straight there
        if DEBUG_MODE:
            print("\n[F8] Accessing MCP data source (Google Sheets) - question routed to specials...")
        try:
            answer = format_specials_answer(specials_for_question(request.question))
        except RuntimeError as e:
            return {"error": str(e)}
        return {
            "cuisine": cuisine,
            "answer": answer,
            "top_match": "(F8) Live data from Google Sheets, not a PDF chunk",
        }
    # ops_intent == "hours" is NOT short-circuited here - standard hours might genuinely be in the PDF
    # menu, so the RAG chain gets first crack at it below; only falls back to F8 if RAG comes up empty.

    memory_config = {"configurable": {"session_id": f"{cuisine}:{request.session_id}"}}  # F7
    # F8: give the RAG chain the resolved date(s) for hours questions (today/tomorrow/a
    # weekday/weekend/etc.), so it can resolve against the PDF's static weekly schedule.
    question_for_chain = with_date_context(request.question) if ops_intent == "hours" else request.question
    # F8: hours questions bypass Ephemeral Chat Memory (F7) entirely - RetrievalQA uses the same
    # (memory-contextualized) text for both retrieval and generation, so prior conversation turns
    # about menu items were diluting the embedding and causing the Hours-of-Operation chunk to miss.
    # Hours lookups are standalone factual questions anyway, so this is a safe, contained bypass.

    def invoke_chain():
        if ops_intent == "hours":
            return qa_chains[cuisine].invoke({"query": question_for_chain})
        return qa_chains_with_memory[cuisine].invoke({"query": question_for_chain}, config=memory_config)  # F7

    if DEBUG_MODE:  # F6: only track usage when the toggle is on
        with track_usage(session_usage_totals) as cb, trace_call(session_trace_totals) as timer:  # F9: retriever/LLM latency
            result = invoke_chain()
        usage = UsageInfo(
            prompt_tokens=cb.prompt_tokens,
            completion_tokens=cb.completion_tokens,
            total_tokens=cb.total_tokens,
            total_cost_usd=cb.total_cost,
        )
        log_call(cuisine, request.session_id, request.question, usage)  # F11: persist this call
        durable_totals = get_session_totals(request.session_id)  # F11: durable totals from usage_log, not memory
    else:  # F6: toggle off - skip tracking entirely
        result = invoke_chain()
        usage = None
        durable_totals = None
        timer = None

    answer = result["result"]
    top_match = result["source_documents"][0].page_content
    if ops_intent == "hours":  # F8: always append any live-sheet exceptions/events for the resolved date(s)
        if DEBUG_MODE:
            print("\n[F8] Accessing MCP data source (Google Sheets) - appending any events for the resolved date(s)...")
        try:
            answer += format_hours_events(hours_for_question(request.question))
        except RuntimeError:
            pass  # F8 lookup failed - keep the RAG answer as-is, nothing to append

    response = {
        "cuisine": cuisine,
        "answer": answer,
        "top_match": top_match,
    }
    if usage is not None:  # F6: only include usage in the response when the toggle is on
        response["usage"] = usage
        response["session_totals"] = durable_totals  # F11: durable, SQL-backed totals (not the in-memory F6 dict)
    if timer is not None:  # F9: only include the latency/error breakdown when the toggle is on
        response["trace"] = {
            "retriever_ms": round(timer.retriever_ms, 1),
            "llm_ms": round(timer.llm_ms, 1),
            "total_ms": round(timer.total_ms, 1),
            "errors": session_trace_totals["errors"],
            "calls": session_trace_totals["calls"],
        }
    return response

@app.get("/specials")
def specials(day: Optional[str] = None):  # F8: same core.sheets logic api/mcp_server.py exposes as an MCP tool
    try:
        return {"specials": get_daily_specials(day)}
    except RuntimeError as e:
        return {"error": str(e)}

@app.get("/hours")
def hours(date: Optional[str] = None):  # F8: same core.sheets logic api/mcp_server.py exposes as an MCP tool
    try:
        return {"hours": get_hours_and_events(date)}
    except RuntimeError as e:
        return {"error": str(e)}

# Only runs when this file is executed directly (python3 menu_api.py),
# not when uvicorn imports it to serve the API
if __name__ == "__main__":
    cuisine = input(f"Which menu cuisine would you like ({'/'.join(available_cuisines)})? ").strip().lower()
    while cuisine not in available_cuisines:
        cuisine = input(f"Please choose one of menu {'/'.join(available_cuisines)}: ").strip().lower()

    qa_chain, docs = build_qa_chain(cuisine)
    qa_chain_with_memory = wrap_with_memory(lambda q: qa_chain.invoke({"query": q}))  # F7
    cli_memory_config = {"configurable": {"session_id": f"{cuisine}:cli"}}  # F7

    # 3.1 Analyze the chunking results: total chunk count and average chunk size
    if DEBUG_MODE:  # F3: test the chunking - print chunk count + average chunk size
        chunk_sizes = [len(doc.page_content) for doc in docs]
        print(f"\nTotal chunks: {len(docs)}")
        print(f"Average chunk size: {sum(chunk_sizes) / len(chunk_sizes):.0f} characters")

    # 3.2 Sample query and top matching result
    query = f"What dishes are on the {cuisine} menu?"
    if DEBUG_MODE:  # F6: track tokens/cost for the CLI sample query too
        with track_usage(session_usage_totals) as cb, trace_call(session_trace_totals) as timer:  # F9
            result = qa_chain_with_memory.invoke({"query": query}, config=cli_memory_config)  # F7
        usage = UsageInfo(
            prompt_tokens=cb.prompt_tokens,
            completion_tokens=cb.completion_tokens,
            total_tokens=cb.total_tokens,
            total_cost_usd=cb.total_cost,
        )
        log_call(cuisine, cli_memory_config["configurable"]["session_id"], query, usage)  # F11: persist this call
        print(f"\n[F6] Tokens - prompt: {cb.prompt_tokens}, completion: {cb.completion_tokens}, "
              f"total: {cb.total_tokens} | Cost: ${cb.total_cost:.6f}")
        print(f"[F11] Session Total (DB) - {get_session_totals(cli_memory_config['configurable']['session_id'])}")
        log_trace(timer, session_trace_totals, label="Sample query")  # F9: retriever/LLM latency + error rate
    else:  # F6: toggle off - skip tracking entirely
        result = qa_chain_with_memory.invoke({"query": query}, config=cli_memory_config)  # F7

    print("\nAnswer:", result["result"])
    print("\n--- Top matching result ---")
    print(result["source_documents"][0].page_content)

    # 3.3 Ask the user a question and get the answer from the RAG chain (loop until 'q' to quit)
    while True:
        user_query = input(f"\nWhat would you like to know about the {cuisine} menu? (q to quit) ")
        if user_query.strip().lower() == "q":
            break
        if user_query.strip().lower() == "tt":  # F11: totals-only shortcut, works regardless of DEBUG_MODE
            print(f"\n[F11] Session Total (DB) - "
                  f"{get_session_totals(cli_memory_config['configurable']['session_id'])}")
            continue
        ops_intent = detect_ops_intent(user_query)  # F8: route obvious specials/hours questions to the live sheet
        if ops_intent == "specials":  # F8: specials only ever live in the sheet, never in the PDF menus - go straight there
            if DEBUG_MODE:
                print("\n[F8] Accessing MCP data source (Google Sheets) - question routed to specials...")
            try:
                print(format_specials_answer(specials_for_question(user_query)))
            except RuntimeError as e:
                print(f"[F8] Error: {e}")
            continue
        # ops_intent == "hours" is NOT short-circuited here - standard hours might genuinely be in the PDF
        # menu, so the RAG chain gets first crack at it below; only falls back to F8 if RAG comes up empty.
        # F8: give the RAG chain the resolved date(s) for hours questions (today/tomorrow/a
        # weekday/weekend/etc.), so it can resolve against the PDF's static weekly schedule.
        query_for_chain = with_date_context(user_query) if ops_intent == "hours" else user_query
        # F8: hours questions bypass Ephemeral Chat Memory (F7) entirely - see the matching note in
        # ask() above for why (prior conversation turns were polluting the retrieval embedding).

        def invoke_chain():
            if ops_intent == "hours":
                return qa_chain.invoke({"query": query_for_chain})
            return qa_chain_with_memory.invoke({"query": query_for_chain}, config=cli_memory_config)  # F7

        if DEBUG_MODE:  # F6: track tokens/cost for each interactive question too
            with track_usage(session_usage_totals) as cb, trace_call(session_trace_totals) as timer:  # F9
                user_result = invoke_chain()
            usage = UsageInfo(
                prompt_tokens=cb.prompt_tokens,
                completion_tokens=cb.completion_tokens,
                total_tokens=cb.total_tokens,
                total_cost_usd=cb.total_cost,
            )
            log_call(cuisine, cli_memory_config["configurable"]["session_id"], user_query, usage)  # F11: persist this call
            print(f"\n[F6] Tokens - prompt: {cb.prompt_tokens}, completion: {cb.completion_tokens}, "
                  f"total: {cb.total_tokens} | Cost: ${cb.total_cost:.6f}")
            print(f"[F11] Session Total (DB) - "
                  f"{get_session_totals(cli_memory_config['configurable']['session_id'])}")
            log_trace(timer, session_trace_totals)  # F9: retriever/LLM latency + error rate
        else:  # F6: toggle off - skip tracking entirely
            user_result = invoke_chain()

        answer = user_result["result"]
        if ops_intent == "hours":  # F8: always append any live-sheet exceptions/events for the resolved date(s)
            if DEBUG_MODE:
                print("\n[F8] Accessing MCP data source (Google Sheets) - appending any events for the resolved date(s)...")
            try:
                answer += format_hours_events(hours_for_question(user_query))
            except RuntimeError as e:
                print(f"[F8] Error: {e}")
        print("\nAnswer:", answer)

# F6 - In-Code Token & Cost Accounting: see FEATURES.md for the full writeup
# (what changed, the general-purpose DEBUG_MODE toggle, and how to run/test it).

Line-by-Line Deep Dive

L39 if os.environ.get("OPENAI_API_KEY"):
Presence check, not validity check — an empty string is falsy in Python, so an accidentally-blank env var correctly falls through to the Azure branch instead of silently "succeeding" with a broken key.
L41-42 ChatOpenAI(model="gpt-4o-mini", ...) / OpenAIEmbeddings(...)
Two separate client objects, not one — chat completion and embeddings are different API endpoints with different pricing and different response shapes, so LangChain models them as separate classes even though both ultimately call OpenAI.
L43-54 Azure branch
Same two-client pattern, but Azure requires an explicit azure_endpoint and deployment_name/deployment — Azure OpenAI resources are deployed per-organization, so there's no single global endpoint the way there is for OpenAI directly.
L55-56 else: raise RuntimeError(...)
Fail fast: this exception fires at module import time — before FAISS indexes are built, before the FastAPI app object even exists — so a missing key produces one clear error line instead of a confusing downstream stack trace from whatever code happens to touch llm first.
L58-63 connectivity test
Gated by DEBUG_MODE. llm.invoke("Say 'connection ok'...") is a real, billed API call — deliberately spending a fraction of a cent to convert "is my key valid" from a question you'd otherwise answer by trial and error into a guaranteed answer within the first second of startup.
Interview angle — "Why not just try/except around the first real request instead?" Because that defers the failure to whichever user happens to ask the first question, and by then you've already paid the cost of building three FAISS indexes. A startup-time check turns "broken in production, discovered by a customer" into "broken in the terminal, discovered in the first second" — the same fail-fast principle a health check endpoint or a Kubernetes readiness probe applies at the infrastructure layer.

Why this exists, in plain English: an LLM can't read an entire PDF menu at once and reliably find the one dish you asked about — so the menu gets cut into small pieces first ("chunks"), and only the most relevant few pieces get shown to the model per question. If the pieces are too big, you waste money and dilute relevance; if they're too small, you lose context (like a dish description getting separated from its price). This check is a quick sanity read on whether that slicing is producing reasonable-sized pieces before trusting anything built on top of it.

Maps to checklist.csv day 3, "RAG & Vectorstore" — confirms the PDF got split into a sane number of reasonably-sized chunks before it's embedded into FAISS.

Where: the __main__ CLI block in menu_api.py (section 3.1), right after build_qa_chain(cuisine) runs for the cuisine you picked.

What it does (gated by if DEBUG_MODE:):

  • prints Total chunks: N — how many chunks RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter produced from the menu PDF
  • prints Average chunk size: X characters — a quick sanity check that chunk size (500 chars, 50 overlap) is behaving as configured

How to test:

source venv/bin/activate
python3 menu_api.py

Pick a cuisine — the two chunk-stat lines print immediately after the vectorstore is built/loaded, before the sample answer. This only runs in the CLI path (not /ask), since that's the only place docs — the raw chunk list — is available; the FastAPI path only keeps the built qa_chain, not the intermediate chunks. Set DEBUG_MODE=false and re-run to confirm the two lines disappear.

#!/usr/bin/env python
# coding: utf-8

# # Demo: Building a RAG-powered FAQ Agent with Custom Knowledge

# Step 1: Install required packages -> see requirements.txt

# Step 2: Import dependencies
import os
from dotenv import load_dotenv, find_dotenv
from langchain_openai import (
    AzureChatOpenAI,
    AzureOpenAIEmbeddings,
    ChatOpenAI,
    OpenAIEmbeddings,
)
from langchain_community.document_loaders import PyPDFLoader
from langchain_text_splitters import RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter
from langchain_community.vectorstores import FAISS
from langchain_classic.chains import RetrievalQA
from langchain_core.prompts import ChatPromptTemplate
from langchain_core.prompts.chat import SystemMessagePromptTemplate, HumanMessagePromptTemplate
from typing import Optional
from fastapi import FastAPI
from pydantic import BaseModel
from core.telemetry import UsageInfo, new_session_totals, track_usage, new_trace_totals, trace_call, log_trace  # F6, F9
from core.memory import wrap_with_memory  # F7
from core.vectorstore import wrap_with_reranking  # F10
from core.database import init_db, log_call, get_session_totals  # F11
from core.sheets import get_daily_specials, get_hours_and_events, detect_ops_intent, resolve_target_days  # F8

# Step 3: Set credentials (loaded from shared .env at the repo root, OpenAI or Azure)
load_dotenv(find_dotenv())

# F2/F3/F6: general debug/testing toggle - set DEBUG_MODE=false in .env to silence
# provider info + connectivity test (F2), chunk stats (F3), and usage/cost tracking (F6)
DEBUG_MODE = os.environ.get("DEBUG_MODE", "true").lower() != "false"

if os.environ.get("OPENAI_API_KEY"):
    provider = "openai"
    llm = ChatOpenAI(model="gpt-4o-mini", temperature=0)
    embeddings = OpenAIEmbeddings(model="text-embedding-3-small")
elif os.environ.get("AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY"):
    provider = "azure"
    llm = AzureChatOpenAI(
        azure_endpoint="https://openai-api-management-gw.azure-api.net",
        api_version="2025-01-01-preview",
        deployment_name="gpt-5-mini",
    )
    embeddings = AzureOpenAIEmbeddings(
        azure_endpoint="https://openai-api-management-gw.azure-api.net",
        api_version="2023-05-15",
        deployment="text-embedding-ada-002",
    )
else:
    raise RuntimeError("Set OPENAI_API_KEY or AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY in the .env file")

if DEBUG_MODE:  # F2: test the LLM - print provider + run a connectivity check
    print(f"Using provider: {provider}")

    # Quick connectivity test — a plain prompt, no FAQ document needed
    test_response = llm.invoke("Say 'connection ok' if you can read this.")
    print("Test prompt response:", test_response.content)

# Full RAG pipeline, wrapped as a reusable function (built once per cuisine, cached by the API below)

# Vectorstore directory
VECTORSTORE_DIR = "vectorstores"

# System prompt for the RAG chain - replaces RetrievalQA's generic default (a bare "use this
# context, say I don't know" instruction) with a consistent restaurant-assistant persona, an
# explicit no-hallucination guardrail, and date-context awareness (matters now that F8 feeds
# this chain resolved dates for hours questions - see with_date_context() below).
RAG_SYSTEM_PROMPT = """You are a friendly, knowledgeable restaurant assistant. Answer guest questions
using ONLY the menu and restaurant information given in the context below - never
invent dishes, prices, ingredients, allergens, or policies that aren't explicitly
there.

Guidelines:
- If the answer isn't in the provided context, say so plainly (e.g. "I don't have
  that information") rather than guessing.
- If the question references a specific date or day (e.g. "today", "Friday",
  "this weekend"), use that to figure out which part of the context applies.
- Keep answers concise and conversational, like speaking to a guest at the
  restaurant - not a bulleted data dump unless they asked for a list.
- Mention prices when referencing specific dishes, if the context gives them.
- If asked about something outside the menu or restaurant policies, politely
  redirect back to what you can help with instead of answering off-topic.
----------------
{context}"""

RAG_PROMPT = ChatPromptTemplate.from_messages([
    SystemMessagePromptTemplate.from_template(RAG_SYSTEM_PROMPT),
    HumanMessagePromptTemplate.from_template("{question}"),
])


def build_qa_chain(cuisine: str):
    menu = f"menus/{cuisine}.pdf"
    # Index path for the vectorstore
    index_path = f"{VECTORSTORE_DIR}/{cuisine}"

    # 2.1 Load and chunk PDFs using PyPDFLoader
    loader = PyPDFLoader(menu)
    documents = loader.load()

    # 2.2 Load and chunk PDFs using RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter
    text_splitter = RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter(chunk_size=500, chunk_overlap=50)
    docs = text_splitter.split_documents(documents)

    # 2.3 Generate embeddings (OpenAI or Azure OpenAI, per provider above) and store in FAISS vectorstore,
    # or load a previously saved index from disk to avoid re-embedding every run
    if os.path.exists(index_path):
        vectorstore = FAISS.load_local(index_path, embeddings, allow_dangerous_deserialization=True)
    else:
        vectorstore = FAISS.from_documents(docs, embeddings)
        vectorstore.save_local(index_path)

    # 2.4 Run retrieval queries with GPT to fetch contextually relevant chunks
    retriever = wrap_with_reranking(vectorstore.as_retriever())  # F10: cross-encoder re-ranks the retrieved chunks
    qa_chain = RetrievalQA.from_chain_type(
        llm=llm,
        retriever=retriever,
        return_source_documents=True,
        chain_type_kwargs={"prompt": RAG_PROMPT},
    )
    return qa_chain, docs


available_cuisines = ["sushi", "steak", "italian"]

qa_chains = {}
docs_by_cuisine = {}
for c in available_cuisines:
    qa_chains[c], docs_by_cuisine[c] = build_qa_chain(c)

qa_chains_with_memory = {}  # F7
for c in available_cuisines:
    qa_chains_with_memory[c] = wrap_with_memory(lambda q, chain=qa_chains[c]: chain.invoke({"query": q}))

app = FastAPI()

session_usage_totals = new_session_totals()  # F6
session_trace_totals = new_trace_totals()  # F9
init_db()  # F11: create usage_log table if it doesn't exist yet

class AskRequest(BaseModel):
    cuisine: str
    question: str
    session_id: str = "default"  # F7

def format_specials_answer(rows: list[dict]) -> str:  # F8: shared by /ask and the CLI
    if not rows:
        return "There are no active specials for that day."
    lines = [f"[{row['Day']}] {row['Dish Name']} ({row['Price']}) - {row['Description']}" for row in rows]
    return "Specials:\n" + "\n".join(lines)

def format_hours_events(rows: list[dict]) -> str:  # F8: shared by /ask and the CLI - "" when there's nothing to append
    if not rows:
        return ""
    lines = [
        f"{row['Date']} ({row['Day']}) - {row['Event / Holiday']}: {row['Status']} "
        f"{row['Open Time']}-{row['Close Time']}"
        for row in rows
    ]
    return "\n\nGoogle Sheets (F8) - holiday/event schedule for that day:\n" + "\n".join(lines)

def specials_for_question(question: str) -> list[dict]:  # F8: resolves tomorrow/weekend/a weekday/etc., dedupes "All Week" rows
    rows, seen = [], set()
    for d in resolve_target_days(question):
        for row in get_daily_specials(d.strftime("%a")):
            if row["Dish Name"] not in seen:
                seen.add(row["Dish Name"])
                rows.append(row)
    return rows

def hours_for_question(question: str) -> list[dict]:  # F8: resolves tomorrow/weekend/a weekday/etc.
    rows = []
    for d in resolve_target_days(question):
        rows.extend(get_hours_and_events(d.isoformat()))
    return rows

def with_date_context(question: str) -> str:  # F8: shared by /ask and the CLI
    # The RAG chain has no way to resolve "today"/"tomorrow"/"this weekend" on its own -
    # the PDF's hours section is a static weekly schedule, so relative-day phrasing fails
    # to resolve without this, even though the schedule itself is in the retrieved chunk.
    target_days = resolve_target_days(question)
    if len(target_days) == 1:
        d = target_days[0]
        prefix = f"The date being asked about is {d.strftime('%A')}, {d.isoformat()}. "
    else:
        parts = ", ".join(f"{d.strftime('%A')} {d.isoformat()}" for d in target_days)
        prefix = f"The dates being asked about are: {parts}. "
    return prefix + question

@app.post("/ask")
def ask(request: AskRequest):
    cuisine = request.cuisine.strip().lower()
    if cuisine not in qa_chains:
        return {"error": f"Unknown cuisine. Choose one of {available_cuisines}"}

    if request.question.strip().lower() == "tt":  # F11: totals-only shortcut, works regardless of DEBUG_MODE
        return {"cuisine": cuisine, "session_totals": get_session_totals(request.session_id)}

    ops_intent = detect_ops_intent(request.question)  # F8: route obvious specials/hours questions to the live sheet
    if ops_intent == "specials":  # F8: specials only ever live in the sheet, never in the PDF menus - go straight there
        if DEBUG_MODE:
            print("\n[F8] Accessing MCP data source (Google Sheets) - question routed to specials...")
        try:
            answer = format_specials_answer(specials_for_question(request.question))
        except RuntimeError as e:
            return {"error": str(e)}
        return {
            "cuisine": cuisine,
            "answer": answer,
            "top_match": "(F8) Live data from Google Sheets, not a PDF chunk",
        }
    # ops_intent == "hours" is NOT short-circuited here - standard hours might genuinely be in the PDF
    # menu, so the RAG chain gets first crack at it below; only falls back to F8 if RAG comes up empty.

    memory_config = {"configurable": {"session_id": f"{cuisine}:{request.session_id}"}}  # F7
    # F8: give the RAG chain the resolved date(s) for hours questions (today/tomorrow/a
    # weekday/weekend/etc.), so it can resolve against the PDF's static weekly schedule.
    question_for_chain = with_date_context(request.question) if ops_intent == "hours" else request.question
    # F8: hours questions bypass Ephemeral Chat Memory (F7) entirely - RetrievalQA uses the same
    # (memory-contextualized) text for both retrieval and generation, so prior conversation turns
    # about menu items were diluting the embedding and causing the Hours-of-Operation chunk to miss.
    # Hours lookups are standalone factual questions anyway, so this is a safe, contained bypass.

    def invoke_chain():
        if ops_intent == "hours":
            return qa_chains[cuisine].invoke({"query": question_for_chain})
        return qa_chains_with_memory[cuisine].invoke({"query": question_for_chain}, config=memory_config)  # F7

    if DEBUG_MODE:  # F6: only track usage when the toggle is on
        with track_usage(session_usage_totals) as cb, trace_call(session_trace_totals) as timer:  # F9: retriever/LLM latency
            result = invoke_chain()
        usage = UsageInfo(
            prompt_tokens=cb.prompt_tokens,
            completion_tokens=cb.completion_tokens,
            total_tokens=cb.total_tokens,
            total_cost_usd=cb.total_cost,
        )
        log_call(cuisine, request.session_id, request.question, usage)  # F11: persist this call
        durable_totals = get_session_totals(request.session_id)  # F11: durable totals from usage_log, not memory
    else:  # F6: toggle off - skip tracking entirely
        result = invoke_chain()
        usage = None
        durable_totals = None
        timer = None

    answer = result["result"]
    top_match = result["source_documents"][0].page_content
    if ops_intent == "hours":  # F8: always append any live-sheet exceptions/events for the resolved date(s)
        if DEBUG_MODE:
            print("\n[F8] Accessing MCP data source (Google Sheets) - appending any events for the resolved date(s)...")
        try:
            answer += format_hours_events(hours_for_question(request.question))
        except RuntimeError:
            pass  # F8 lookup failed - keep the RAG answer as-is, nothing to append

    response = {
        "cuisine": cuisine,
        "answer": answer,
        "top_match": top_match,
    }
    if usage is not None:  # F6: only include usage in the response when the toggle is on
        response["usage"] = usage
        response["session_totals"] = durable_totals  # F11: durable, SQL-backed totals (not the in-memory F6 dict)
    if timer is not None:  # F9: only include the latency/error breakdown when the toggle is on
        response["trace"] = {
            "retriever_ms": round(timer.retriever_ms, 1),
            "llm_ms": round(timer.llm_ms, 1),
            "total_ms": round(timer.total_ms, 1),
            "errors": session_trace_totals["errors"],
            "calls": session_trace_totals["calls"],
        }
    return response

@app.get("/specials")
def specials(day: Optional[str] = None):  # F8: same core.sheets logic api/mcp_server.py exposes as an MCP tool
    try:
        return {"specials": get_daily_specials(day)}
    except RuntimeError as e:
        return {"error": str(e)}

@app.get("/hours")
def hours(date: Optional[str] = None):  # F8: same core.sheets logic api/mcp_server.py exposes as an MCP tool
    try:
        return {"hours": get_hours_and_events(date)}
    except RuntimeError as e:
        return {"error": str(e)}

# Only runs when this file is executed directly (python3 menu_api.py),
# not when uvicorn imports it to serve the API
if __name__ == "__main__":
    cuisine = input(f"Which menu cuisine would you like ({'/'.join(available_cuisines)})? ").strip().lower()
    while cuisine not in available_cuisines:
        cuisine = input(f"Please choose one of menu {'/'.join(available_cuisines)}: ").strip().lower()

    qa_chain, docs = build_qa_chain(cuisine)
    qa_chain_with_memory = wrap_with_memory(lambda q: qa_chain.invoke({"query": q}))  # F7
    cli_memory_config = {"configurable": {"session_id": f"{cuisine}:cli"}}  # F7

    # 3.1 Analyze the chunking results: total chunk count and average chunk size
    if DEBUG_MODE:  # F3: test the chunking - print chunk count + average chunk size
        chunk_sizes = [len(doc.page_content) for doc in docs]
        print(f"\nTotal chunks: {len(docs)}")
        print(f"Average chunk size: {sum(chunk_sizes) / len(chunk_sizes):.0f} characters")

    # 3.2 Sample query and top matching result
    query = f"What dishes are on the {cuisine} menu?"
    if DEBUG_MODE:  # F6: track tokens/cost for the CLI sample query too
        with track_usage(session_usage_totals) as cb, trace_call(session_trace_totals) as timer:  # F9
            result = qa_chain_with_memory.invoke({"query": query}, config=cli_memory_config)  # F7
        usage = UsageInfo(
            prompt_tokens=cb.prompt_tokens,
            completion_tokens=cb.completion_tokens,
            total_tokens=cb.total_tokens,
            total_cost_usd=cb.total_cost,
        )
        log_call(cuisine, cli_memory_config["configurable"]["session_id"], query, usage)  # F11: persist this call
        print(f"\n[F6] Tokens - prompt: {cb.prompt_tokens}, completion: {cb.completion_tokens}, "
              f"total: {cb.total_tokens} | Cost: ${cb.total_cost:.6f}")
        print(f"[F11] Session Total (DB) - {get_session_totals(cli_memory_config['configurable']['session_id'])}")
        log_trace(timer, session_trace_totals, label="Sample query")  # F9: retriever/LLM latency + error rate
    else:  # F6: toggle off - skip tracking entirely
        result = qa_chain_with_memory.invoke({"query": query}, config=cli_memory_config)  # F7

    print("\nAnswer:", result["result"])
    print("\n--- Top matching result ---")
    print(result["source_documents"][0].page_content)

    # 3.3 Ask the user a question and get the answer from the RAG chain (loop until 'q' to quit)
    while True:
        user_query = input(f"\nWhat would you like to know about the {cuisine} menu? (q to quit) ")
        if user_query.strip().lower() == "q":
            break
        if user_query.strip().lower() == "tt":  # F11: totals-only shortcut, works regardless of DEBUG_MODE
            print(f"\n[F11] Session Total (DB) - "
                  f"{get_session_totals(cli_memory_config['configurable']['session_id'])}")
            continue
        ops_intent = detect_ops_intent(user_query)  # F8: route obvious specials/hours questions to the live sheet
        if ops_intent == "specials":  # F8: specials only ever live in the sheet, never in the PDF menus - go straight there
            if DEBUG_MODE:
                print("\n[F8] Accessing MCP data source (Google Sheets) - question routed to specials...")
            try:
                print(format_specials_answer(specials_for_question(user_query)))
            except RuntimeError as e:
                print(f"[F8] Error: {e}")
            continue
        # ops_intent == "hours" is NOT short-circuited here - standard hours might genuinely be in the PDF
        # menu, so the RAG chain gets first crack at it below; only falls back to F8 if RAG comes up empty.
        # F8: give the RAG chain the resolved date(s) for hours questions (today/tomorrow/a
        # weekday/weekend/etc.), so it can resolve against the PDF's static weekly schedule.
        query_for_chain = with_date_context(user_query) if ops_intent == "hours" else user_query
        # F8: hours questions bypass Ephemeral Chat Memory (F7) entirely - see the matching note in
        # ask() above for why (prior conversation turns were polluting the retrieval embedding).

        def invoke_chain():
            if ops_intent == "hours":
                return qa_chain.invoke({"query": query_for_chain})
            return qa_chain_with_memory.invoke({"query": query_for_chain}, config=cli_memory_config)  # F7

        if DEBUG_MODE:  # F6: track tokens/cost for each interactive question too
            with track_usage(session_usage_totals) as cb, trace_call(session_trace_totals) as timer:  # F9
                user_result = invoke_chain()
            usage = UsageInfo(
                prompt_tokens=cb.prompt_tokens,
                completion_tokens=cb.completion_tokens,
                total_tokens=cb.total_tokens,
                total_cost_usd=cb.total_cost,
            )
            log_call(cuisine, cli_memory_config["configurable"]["session_id"], user_query, usage)  # F11: persist this call
            print(f"\n[F6] Tokens - prompt: {cb.prompt_tokens}, completion: {cb.completion_tokens}, "
                  f"total: {cb.total_tokens} | Cost: ${cb.total_cost:.6f}")
            print(f"[F11] Session Total (DB) - "
                  f"{get_session_totals(cli_memory_config['configurable']['session_id'])}")
            log_trace(timer, session_trace_totals)  # F9: retriever/LLM latency + error rate
        else:  # F6: toggle off - skip tracking entirely
            user_result = invoke_chain()

        answer = user_result["result"]
        if ops_intent == "hours":  # F8: always append any live-sheet exceptions/events for the resolved date(s)
            if DEBUG_MODE:
                print("\n[F8] Accessing MCP data source (Google Sheets) - appending any events for the resolved date(s)...")
            try:
                answer += format_hours_events(hours_for_question(user_query))
            except RuntimeError as e:
                print(f"[F8] Error: {e}")
        print("\nAnswer:", answer)

# F6 - In-Code Token & Cost Accounting: see FEATURES.md for the full writeup
# (what changed, the general-purpose DEBUG_MODE toggle, and how to run/test it).

Line-by-Line Deep Dive

L103-105 PyPDFLoader(menu).load()
One Document per PDF page — the raw unit before any chunking happens. A 3-page menu becomes 3 documents here, each potentially thousands of characters long.
L108 RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter(chunk_size=500, chunk_overlap=50)
Why "recursive": this splitter tries a list of separators in priority order (paragraph breaks, then line breaks, then sentences, then words) and only falls back to a harder cut when a piece still doesn't fit — it prefers breaking at natural boundaries over breaking mid-sentence. chunk_overlap=50 means each chunk repeats the last 50 characters of the previous one, so a detail near a chunk boundary (a price right after a dish name, say) doesn't get orphaned into a chunk that's missing its own context.
L109 text_splitter.split_documents(documents)
Turns the page-level documents into the actual chunk list (docs) — this is what gets embedded into FAISS, and it's the number this section's stats print is checking.
L305-309 chunk-stats print
len(docs) is the chunk count; average chunk size is computed directly from len(doc.page_content) for every chunk, not estimated — a fast, honest sanity check with no external dependency, run only in the CLI path where the raw docs list is still in scope (the FastAPI startup path discards it once qa_chain is built).
Interview angle — "How did you pick 500/50 for chunk size and overlap?" There's a real trade-off here: bigger chunks preserve more context per retrieval but dilute relevance (a big chunk with one relevant sentence and four irrelevant ones still "matches" a query, wasting context-window budget on noise); smaller chunks are more precise but risk splitting a fact away from the context that explains it. 500 characters with 50 overlap is a reasonable default for short, dense text like a menu (a dish + description + price usually fits in ~500 characters), and it's the kind of parameter you'd validate empirically against Hit Rate / Context Precision — see Automated RAG Evals Harness (F17) — rather than assume is correct forever.

↑ Back to top

F3.1 — RAG System Prompt & Persona

Not one of the original 21 checklist days — added while testing F8, and worth tracking anyway: it isn't scoped to F8 at all. It changes the core RAG chain itself, so it affects every question, on all three cuisines, not just hours/specials routing. Added to checklist.csv/checklist.html as day 3.1, right after RAG & Vectorstore (F3), since it's a real, shipped change with its own toolbox and metrics that lives in the same RAG-chain layer, even though it wasn't part of the original spec.

Where: menu_api.py, right above build_qa_chain().

Why: RetrievalQA.from_chain_type() was using LangChain's built-in default prompt — for a chat model, that's already a real system/human message split (confirmed by reading langchain_classic.chains.question_answering.stuff_prompt directly), but the system message is just a generic "use this context, say I don't know" instruction with no persona, no hallucination guardrail beyond the bare minimum, and no awareness that a question might reference a specific date — which matters now that F8 feeds this same chain resolved dates for hours questions via with_date_context().

What it does:

  • gives the assistant a consistent restaurant persona ("friendly, knowledgeable") instead of a generic Q&A tone, across all three cuisines
  • reinforces the no-hallucination guardrail explicitly: never invent dishes, prices, ingredients, allergens, or policies not in the retrieved context
  • tells the model how to use date-referencing questions ("today", "Friday", "this weekend") against the context it's given — directly supports F8's hours flow
  • asks for concise, conversational answers instead of a bulleted data dump by default
  • adds an explicit off-topic redirect instruction, instead of leaving that behavior to whatever the base model does by default

How to test:

source venv/bin/activate
uvicorn menu_api:app --reload --port 8000
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/ask -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"cuisine": "sushi", "question": "what is the capital of France"}'

Confirms the off-topic redirect guideline: expect something like "I don't have that information. However, if you have any questions about our menu or dishes, I'm here to help!" instead of the model actually answering about France. Compare against a normal menu question (e.g. "what rolls do you have") to see the persona/tone and price-mentioning guidelines in the same response style.

Source: menu_api.py (RAG_SYSTEM_PROMPT / RAG_PROMPT)

# System prompt for the RAG chain - replaces RetrievalQA's generic default (a bare "use this
# context, say I don't know" instruction) with a consistent restaurant-assistant persona, an
# explicit no-hallucination guardrail, and date-context awareness (matters now that F8 feeds
# this chain resolved dates for hours questions - see with_date_context() below).
RAG_SYSTEM_PROMPT = """You are a friendly, knowledgeable restaurant assistant. Answer guest questions
using ONLY the menu and restaurant information given in the context below - never
invent dishes, prices, ingredients, allergens, or policies that aren't explicitly
there.

Guidelines:
- If the answer isn't in the provided context, say so plainly (e.g. "I don't have
  that information") rather than guessing.
- If the question references a specific date or day (e.g. "today", "Friday",
  "this weekend"), use that to figure out which part of the context applies.
- Keep answers concise and conversational, like speaking to a guest at the
  restaurant - not a bulleted data dump unless they asked for a list.
- Mention prices when referencing specific dishes, if the context gives them.
- If asked about something outside the menu or restaurant policies, politely
  redirect back to what you can help with instead of answering off-topic.
----------------
{context}"""

RAG_PROMPT = ChatPromptTemplate.from_messages([
    SystemMessagePromptTemplate.from_template(RAG_SYSTEM_PROMPT),
    HumanMessagePromptTemplate.from_template("{question}"),
])

This snippet lives inside menu_api.py — see the full file under F2 or F4 above/below for everything around it.

Line-by-Line Deep Dive

RAG_SYSTEM_PROMPT string
A plain multi-line string, not a LangChain object yet — the {context} placeholder at the end gets filled in later by RetrievalQA with the retrieved chunks. Five separate guidelines are spelled out explicitly (don't guess, use date context, stay conversational, mention prices, redirect off-topic questions) rather than left implicit, because a chat model's default behavior on each of these is inconsistent call to call without an explicit instruction.
ChatPromptTemplate.from_messages([...])
Builds a real system + human message pair instead of one flat string. Why this matters technically: chat models are trained to weight system-role instructions differently (and more durably against later user input) than a plain user-role instruction — folding the persona/guardrail text into the human message instead would make it easier for a crafted question to override.
chain_type_kwargs={"prompt": RAG_PROMPT} (in build_qa_chain, F2/F4's full listing)
This is the actual wiring point — without passing prompt here, RetrievalQA silently falls back to LangChain's generic built-in QA prompt, and none of the persona/guardrail text would ever reach the model.
Interview angle — "Why is this its own checklist item instead of just part of F3?" Because it's a cross-cutting change to the chain's behavior itself (every question, every cuisine), not a one-time pipeline-construction step like chunking. It also has its own testable failure mode (off-topic questions getting real answers instead of a redirect) and its own metrics (Off-Topic Redirect Rate, Hallucination Rate) — tracking it separately keeps "did chunking work" and "does the assistant behave correctly" as two distinct, independently verifiable claims.

Why this exists, in plain English: a script that only runs in one person's terminal isn't a product — nobody else can use it. Wrapping the same pipeline in a web API means any client (a browser page, a mobile app, another service, a teammate's curl command) can ask the assistant a question the same standard way, over HTTP, without needing Python installed or the FAISS indexes on their own machine. This is the line where the project stops being a personal script and starts being something that could actually be deployed.

Maps to checklist.csv day 4, "FastAPI" — wraps the same RAG pipeline the CLI uses (F1–F3) in an HTTP API instead of a terminal loop.

Where: menu_api.py — the FastAPI app object and its POST /ask endpoint.

What it does:

  • builds/loads all 3 cuisines' FAISS vectorstores once at startup (via build_qa_chain() per cuisine), so a request never pays the chunk/embed cost — only the retrieval + LLM call
  • POST /ask accepts {"cuisine": ..., "question": ...} and returns {"cuisine", "answer", "top_match"} (plus usage/session_totals once In-Code Token & Cost Accounting (F6)/Relational DB & Text-to-SQL Tool (F11) are wired in — see below)
  • this is the endpoint every other client in this doc talks to — curl, Postman, and both web UIs (F5)

How to test:

source venv/bin/activate
uvicorn menu_api:app --reload --port 8000
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/ask \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"cuisine": "sushi", "question": "What rolls are on the menu?"}'

Watch for Application startup complete in the uvicorn terminal first, then confirm the curl response includes answer and top_match. Same endpoint also underlies every /ask call used to test F5–F7/F10/F11 below.
