F12:1 Modular Engine Strategy Factory: One Fixed Chain Isn't Enough Anymore: Building the Plug Before the Appliances

Until now, menu_api.py's /ask route does exactly one thing: build a RetrievalQA chain and call .invoke() on it — hardcoded, no seam anywhere. But the next three checklist days want to plug in completely different ways of answering the same question: LangGraph State Machine Engine (F13) wants a graph with conditional edges and retry loops, CrewAI Multi-Role Engine (F14) wants a small team of specialized agents, AutoGen Multi-Agent Engine (F15) wants two agents debating an answer. Wiring each of those in as another if/elif inside /ask would work today but turns that route into a growing pile of engine-specific logic that gets worse with every addition.

Modular Engine Strategy Factory is the Strategy design pattern applied to "how do we answer a question": one abstract interface (BaseMenuEngine) that every concrete answering strategy implements identically, and one factory function (get_engine) that hands back whichever concrete strategy was asked for, by name. Callers only ever talk to the interface — they have no idea, and no need to know, whether they're holding a plain RAG chain, a LangGraph state machine, or a CrewAI crew.

The one engine that exists behind the factory today, PlainRagEngine, isn't new logic — it's the exact same RAG chain (F3/F3.1/F7/F10) menu_api.py already runs, reimplemented behind the new interface. F12's whole job is proving the seam works with zero behavior change before any new engine exists, which is also exactly what its own metrics (Framework Switching Latency, Engine Throughput) are meant to catch — this abstraction should cost close to nothing.

The Big Picture: How the Architecture Works

At a high level, the strategy factory breaks "answering a question" into three responsibilities:

  • The Contract (BaseMenuEngine): an abstract base class with exactly one method, answer(cuisine, question, session_id, use_memory) — every engine, present and future, implements this one method and nothing else is assumed about how it works internally.
  • The Factory (get_engine function): given a name, returns the matching engine instance — built once, cached as a singleton, and returned as-is on every later call so FAISS indexes and provider clients aren't rebuilt per request.
  • The Implementation (PlainRagEngine): the first (and so far only) concrete engine — RAG system prompt, per-cuisine RetrievalQA chains, and memory wrapping, implemented as methods on a class that satisfies the contract above. Provider setup and retriever construction aren't reimplemented here at all — they're shared helpers (core/llm.py, core/vectorstore.py) every engine calls into instead of duplicating; see "Where the Shared Helpers Plug In" below.

What's Imported (and Why)

  • abc.ABC, abc.abstractmethod (Python standard library) — the entire interface mechanism. No third-party dependency needed for a Strategy pattern this small.
  • engines/plain_rag_engine.py imports nothing new either — it's the same langchain_classic/langchain_core RAG-chain/persona stack Test the chunking (F3) and Test the API (F4) already use, plus three shared helpers: core.llm.build_llm_and_embeddings (provider selection, F2), core.vectorstore.get_retriever (the FAISS load-or-build pipeline, F3/F10), and core.memory.wrap_with_memory (Ephemeral Chat Memory, F7) — the engine wraps existing building blocks, it doesn't add any.
  • engine_api.py (F12.1, below) imports core.telemetry (In-Code Token & Cost Accounting F6 / Observability & Tracing F9), core.database (Relational DB & Text-to-SQL Tool F11), and core.sheets (FastMCP Server Endpoint F8) — the same shared modules menu_api.py already depends on, imported a second time by a sibling file rather than shared code (see the trade-off below).

For the full, step-by-step code implementation, class structures, and technical configuration, please refer to the GitHub Repository & Code Details link.

Tags: Software Architecture, Strategy Pattern, Factory Pattern, F12

Tools & Libraries (per checklist.csv's "Primary Tools & Libraries" for #12):
  • BaseMenuEngine (custom ABC) — used. One abstract method, answer(...) — the entire contract every engine (this one and F13/F14/F15) has to satisfy.
  • Factory (custom function) — used, but as a plain function returning from a name-keyed dict, not a formal Abstract Factory class hierarchy. With one engine today and three more planned, a dict dispatch plus a singleton cache is enough — a full Factory/AbstractFactory class pair would add a layer of indirection for no real benefit at this scale, the same reasoning Relational DB & Text-to-SQL Tool (F11) used to skip an ORM for one table.

Modules: engines/base.py, engines/plain_rag_engine.py (both new files) — matches checklist.csv's Target Location for #12. Plus engine_api.py (new file, project root) for #12.1, below.

Modular Engine Strategy Factory (F12) doesn't replace any prior work — PlainRagEngine still runs the exact same RAG chain RAG System Prompt & Persona (F3.1), Ephemeral Chat Memory (F7), and Cross-Encoder Re-ranking (F10) already built. F12 only adds a seam around that existing chain so LangGraph State Machine Engine (F13), CrewAI Multi-Role Engine (F14), and AutoGen Multi-Agent Engine (F15) can each become a sibling of PlainRagEngine later instead of a rewrite of /ask.
Revisited after F12 shipped, while scoping F13: PlainRagEngine originally carried its own private copy of provider selection (_build_llm_and_embeddings()) and the FAISS load-or-build pipeline inline in _build_qa_chain() — duplicated from menu_api.py on purpose, per F12's "prove the seam first" goal. But LangGraph State Machine Engine (F13) needs that exact same provider setup and retriever, and a third copy of ~30 identical lines was the wrong kind of duplication: unlike the RAG chain/persona (genuinely different per engine), the FAISS pipeline is identical infrastructure every engine needs. Both pieces moved out to be shared: core/llm.py (new file) now owns build_llm_and_embeddings(), and core/vectorstore.py gained get_retriever(cuisine, embeddings) alongside Cross-Encoder Re-ranking (F10)'s existing wrap_with_reranking. PlainRagEngine shrank from 130 to 76 lines with zero behavior change — it now imports both instead of duplicating them. menu_api.py's own inline copies of both stay exactly as they were; only the two engine-facing copies were collapsed into one.

Where the Shared Helpers Plug In

Class: BaseMenuEngine(ABC) — one abstract method: answer(cuisine: str, question: str, session_id: str, use_memory: bool = True) -> dict, returning {"result": str, "source_documents": [...]} — the same shape RetrievalQA.invoke() already returns, so nothing downstream of an engine call needed to change shape.

Function: get_engine(name: str) -> BaseMenuEngine — checks a module-level _engine_instances cache first; on a miss, lazily imports the matching engine class (so engines/base.py never needs the other engine modules to exist just to be importable), instantiates it once, caches it, and returns it. Raises ValueError for an unrecognized name.

Class: PlainRagEngine(BaseMenuEngine) — on construction, builds the provider clients via core.llm.build_llm_and_embeddings() (OpenAI or Azure, same selection logic as menu_api.py) and eagerly builds a RetrievalQA chain (its retriever from core.vectorstore.get_retriever()) plus a memory-wrapped variant for every cuisine, exactly like menu_api.py's startup loop does. answer(...) routes to the memory-wrapped chain or the plain chain depending on use_memory — the same hours-questions-bypass-memory branch FastMCP Server Endpoint (F8) needs.

Request Trace: Answering a Question, Start to End (Non-Agentic / F12)

Tracing one POST /ask call for engine: "plain_rag" through every file it touches, in order:

  • engine_api.py — POST /ask → ask(request)
    • validates cuisine, handles the "tt" totals-shortcut early
    • core/sheets.py: detect_ops_intent(question) — classifies specials / hours / menu
      • "specials" → short-circuits straight to Google Sheets, never touches an engine at all
    • with_date_context(question) if hours-intent (injects the resolved date into the question text)
    • engines/base.py: get_engine("plain_rag")
      • first call only: lazily imports engines/plain_rag_engine.py, instantiates PlainRagEngine(), caches it in _engine_instances
  • engines/plain_rag_engine.py — PlainRagEngine.__init__() (only runs once, on that first get_engine call)
    • core/llm.py: build_llm_and_embeddings() → returns (llm, embeddings)
    • for each cuisine, _build_qa_chain(cuisine):
      • core/vectorstore.py: get_retriever(cuisine, embeddings)
        • checks vectorstores/{cuisine}/ on disk — exists → FAISS.load_local(...); missing → PyPDFLoader on menus/{cuisine}.pdf → RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter → FAISS.from_documents(...) → .save_local(...)
        • wrap_with_reranking(...) → returns a RerankingRetriever
      • RetrievalQA.from_chain_type(llm, retriever, RAG_PROMPT) → the per-cuisine chain
    • core/memory.py: wrap_with_memory(...) → the memory-wrapped variant of that same chain
  • back in engine_api.py — engine.answer(cuisine, question, session_id, use_memory)
  • engines/plain_rag_engine.py — PlainRagEngine.answer(...)
    • use_memory=False (hours questions) → qa_chains[cuisine].invoke({"query": question}) directly
    • use_memory=True (everything else) → qa_chains_with_memory[cuisine].invoke(...)
      • core/memory.py — get_session_history(session_id), prepends prior turns, calls the underlying chain, then records the new exchange
    • either way, underneath it's the same RetrievalQA chain invoking:
      • core/vectorstore.py — RerankingRetriever._get_relevant_documents() → base FAISS retriever → rerank_documents() (flashrank cross-encoder) → top-k docs
      • the LLM call itself (self.llm, from core/llm.py's client), using RAG_PROMPT with those docs as {context}
    • returns {"result": "...", "source_documents": [...]}
  • back in engine_api.py — still inside ask(...)
    • core/telemetry.py — track_usage/trace_call wrapped around the whole invoke_engine() call (tokens, cost, retriever/LLM latency)
    • core/database.py — log_call(...) persists the call, get_session_totals(...) reads back durable totals
    • if hours-intent: core/sheets.py — hours_for_question() → get_hours_and_events(), appended onto the answer text
    • assembles and returns the final JSON: {cuisine, answer, top_match, engine, usage?, session_totals?, trace?}

Seven files touched by one request, with PlainRagEngine.__init__() — and therefore core/llm.py/core/vectorstore.py — only running once per process, not once per request.

Request Trace: Agentic Flow (F13)

The trace above is one path the factory routes to. Here's the same shape of trace for engine: "langgraph", per LangGraph State Machine Engine (F13, detailed further in F13's own section below) — shown here, side by side with the non-agentic trace above, because the whole point of Modular Engine Strategy Factory (F12) is that this second trace only had to add one new file, not rebuild the pipeline around it:

  • engine_api.py — same entry as the non-agentic path, up through get_engine("langgraph")
    • lazily imports engines/langgraph_engine.py, instantiates LangGraphEngine(), caches it
  • engines/langgraph_engine.py — LangGraphEngine.__init__() (once per process)
    • core/llm.py: build_llm_and_embeddings() — identical call to the non-agentic path
    • per cuisine, core/vectorstore.py: get_retriever(cuisine, embeddings) — same shared retriever, no duplicate FAISS pipeline
    • _build_graph() — wires a StateGraph: route → (retrieve | redirect), retrieve → generate → verify, verify → (retrieve again | done), compiled once per cuisine
    • core/memory.py: wrap_with_memory(...) — same memory wrapping as above, around the whole graph invocation
  • engines/langgraph_engine.py — LangGraphEngine.answer(...)
    • use_memory=False (hours questions) → invokes the compiled graph directly, same branch the non-agentic path uses
    • use_memory=True → through core/memory.py's wrapper first, exactly like PlainRagEngine.answer(...)
    • either way, running the compiled graph means:
      • _route_node — a structured LLM call (RouteDecision) classifying on-topic vs. off-topic — the "more principled" replacement for F8's detect_ops_intent the checklist calls for
      • off-topic → _redirect_node — canned redirect, no retrieval or generation spent → graph ends
      • on-topic → _retrieve_node — the same core/vectorstore.py retriever as the non-agentic path (FAISS + F10's cross-encoder re-ranking)
      • _generate_node — an LLM call against RAG_PROMPT plus the retrieved context; on a retry, folds the verifier's rejection reason into the question so the second attempt has something concrete to fix
      • _verify_node — a second structured LLM call (VerifyDecision) grading whether the answer is actually grounded in the retrieved context
        • grounded, or attempts has reached MAX_RETRIES → graph ends
        • not grounded and retries remain → loops back to _retrieve_node — the bounded self-correction loop
    • returns {"result": ..., "source_documents": ...} — the same shape PlainRagEngine.answer() returns, so nothing downstream needs to know which engine answered
  • back in engine_api.py — identical to the non-agentic path from here: core/telemetry.py usage/latency tracking, core/database.py call logging, an hours-append via core/sheets.py if needed, then the final JSON response (now with "engine": "langgraph")

Line up the two traces and the only genuinely new file is engines/langgraph_engine.py and the graph nodes inside it — every other file in the agentic trace is a file the non-agentic trace already runs. That's the payoff Modular Engine Strategy Factory (F12) was built for.

↑ Back to F12

F12:3 Integration Guide: Integration: engine_api.py (F12.1 — Parallel Entry Point)

Not one of the original 21 checklist days — added while implementing F12, and worth tracking on its own line rather than folding silently into F12: the original plan assumed /ask in menu_api.py itself would get updated to call get_engine(...) directly. Instead, menu_api.py stays completely untouched, by explicit choice — kept around as a known-good, always-runnable baseline (python3 menu_api.py / uvicorn menu_api:app still work exactly as before, unaffected by anything below). Everything that depends on the new factory lives in a second, parallel FastAPI app instead. Added to checklist.csv/checklist.html as day 12.1, right after Modular Engine Strategy Factory (F12).

Trade-off: FastMCP Server Endpoint (F8)'s ops-intent helpers (format_specials_answer, format_hours_events, specials_for_question, hours_for_question, with_date_context), the /specials//hours routes, and the CLI loop are all duplicated between menu_api.py and engine_api.py rather than shared, since sharing them would mean editing menu_api.py. The two files' F8 logic has to be kept in sync by hand going forward — the System Prompt & Persona (F3.1) guideline about stating specific policy details, added mid-session, already had to be applied to both files for exactly this reason.

  • same AskRequest shape as menu_api.py, plus one new optional field: engine: Optional[str] = None (a per-request override of DEFAULT_ENGINE)
  • reads DEFAULT_ENGINE from .env (defaults to "plain_rag") and calls get_engine(request.engine or DEFAULT_ENGINE) instead of invoking a chain directly
  • echoes back which engine answered in the response ("engine": "plain_rag"), so this becomes visible once LangGraph State Machine Engine (F13)/CrewAI Multi-Role Engine (F14)/AutoGen Multi-Agent Engine (F15) exist and are selectable per-request
  • the CLI (python3 engine_api.py) always uses DEFAULT_ENGINE — no per-call override there, unlike /ask

↑ Back to F12

F12:4 Testing Guide: How to test Modular Engine Strategy Factory (F12) / Parallel Entry Point (F12.1)

1) CLI — same interactive loop as menu_api.py, answering through the factory:

source venv/bin/activate
python3 engine_api.py

Pick a cuisine and, if DEBUG_MODE is on, an engine (Enter for DEFAULT_ENGINE, or 2 for LangGraph), then ask a question. Run python3 menu_api.py separately (before or after) with the same question to confirm the two give the same answer and neither affects the other's state.

2) FastAPI — curl, Postman, or the Gradio/Streamlit UIs are three ways to hit the same engine_api:app backend; start it once, then use whichever client you like:

uvicorn engine_api:app --reload --port 8000

curl — confirms the factory path end-to-end:

curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/ask -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"cuisine": "sushi", "question": "What rolls do you have?"}'

The response includes "engine": "plain_rag", proving /ask went through get_engine("plain_rag").answer(...) rather than a hardcoded chain. Pass engine explicitly in the request body to override DEFAULT_ENGINE per-call — "engine": "plain_rag" gives the same answer as above, and now that LangGraph State Machine Engine (F13) exists, "engine": "langgraph" is a second real, working value (see F13's own "How to test" section). Passing a truly unrecognized name (e.g. "engine": "made_up") still raises an uncaught ValueError inside get_engine, which FastAPI turns into a raw 500 — there's no friendly {"error": ...} response for an unknown engine name yet, unlike the unknown-cuisine case a few lines above it in /ask.

Postman — same request, no terminal needed: method POST, URL http://127.0.0.1:8000/ask, a Content-Type: application/json header, and the same JSON above pasted into the raw request body. Useful for saving a few cuisine/engine/question combinations as a reusable collection instead of retyping curl commands.

Gradio / Streamlit (both need the uvicorn server above running):

python3 web-demo/gradio_app.py
# or
streamlit run web-demo/streamlit_app.py

Both UIs talk to whichever backend is listening on port 8000 without any code change — point them at engine_api:app instead of menu_api:app and they work identically, since the request/response shapes match. Neither UI exposes an engine selector, so both always answer through DEFAULT_ENGINE — use curl/Postman's per-request engine override above to test a specific engine through the UI layer. Give each browser session its own session_id rather than leaving it unset — every UI session currently shares the same "default" memory bucket, and a busy shared session can dilute retrieval for short, ambiguous questions (see the deep dive below).

# F12: Modular Engine Strategy Factory - the shared plug/socket every "engine" (plain RAG today,
# LangGraph/CrewAI/AutoGen later) implements the same way, so callers never depend on a concrete
# engine class directly - only on this interface and the factory below.
from abc import ABC, abstractmethod


class BaseMenuEngine(ABC):  # F12: common interface every engine implements
    @abstractmethod
    def answer(self, cuisine: str, question: str, session_id: str, use_memory: bool = True) -> dict:
        """Returns {"result": str, "source_documents": [Document, ...]} - same shape RetrievalQA.invoke() returns."""


_engine_instances: dict[str, BaseMenuEngine] = {}  # F12: cached singletons, keyed by engine name - built once, reused


def get_engine(name: str) -> BaseMenuEngine:  # F12: factory - returns the requested engine, building it on first use
    if name not in _engine_instances:
        if name == "plain_rag":
            from engines.plain_rag_engine import PlainRagEngine  # lazy import - avoids a hard dependency at module load
            _engine_instances[name] = PlainRagEngine()
        else:
            raise ValueError(f"Unknown engine: {name}")
    return _engine_instances[name]

# F12: shared LLM/embeddings provider selection - used by every engine (plain_rag today,
# langgraph/crewai/autogen later) instead of each duplicating its own copy. menu_api.py and
# menu_rag.py keep their own inline copies, untouched, on purpose.
import os

from langchain_openai import (  # F2: LLM Selector - OpenAI or Azure
    AzureChatOpenAI,
    AzureOpenAIEmbeddings,
    ChatOpenAI,
    OpenAIEmbeddings,
)


# Other params available on ChatOpenAI/AzureChatOpenAI, for future reference
# (full list: https://platform.openai.com/docs/api-reference/chat/create):
#   max_tokens=500          - hard cap on response length (cost/latency control)
#   top_p=1.0               - nucleus sampling, alternative/complement to temperature
#   frequency_penalty=0.0   - >0 discourages repeating the same tokens
#   presence_penalty=0.0    - >0 encourages introducing new topics/words
#   timeout=30              - seconds before the request gives up
#   max_retries=2           - retries on transient API errors
#   seed=42                 - best-effort reproducibility across calls (not fully guaranteed)
def build_llm_and_embeddings():  # F2/F12: same provider selection every engine needs
    if os.environ.get("OPENAI_API_KEY"):
        llm = ChatOpenAI(model="gpt-4o-mini", temperature=0)  # 0 = deterministic/focused; default is 1.0
        return llm, OpenAIEmbeddings(model="text-embedding-3-small")
    elif os.environ.get("AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY"):  # F2
        llm = AzureChatOpenAI(
            azure_endpoint="https://openai-api-management-gw.azure-api.net",
            api_version="2025-01-01-preview",
            deployment_name="gpt-5-mini",
            temperature=0,  # matches the OpenAI branch above; default is 1.0 if unset
        )
        embeddings = AzureOpenAIEmbeddings(
            azure_endpoint="https://openai-api-management-gw.azure-api.net",
            api_version="2023-05-15",
            deployment="text-embedding-ada-002",
        )
        return llm, embeddings
    else:
        raise RuntimeError("Set OPENAI_API_KEY or AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY in the .env file")

# F12: the plain-RAG engine - same RetrievalQA logic menu_api.py already runs, reimplemented
# here as its own module behind BaseMenuEngine. menu_api.py is left untouched on purpose.
# Provider selection (core.llm) and the FAISS load-or-build pipeline (core.vectorstore) are
# shared with other engines (F13+) instead of duplicated here; the RAG chain/persona below,
# and menu_api.py's own copies of both, are each engine's/file's own.
from dotenv import load_dotenv, find_dotenv
from langchain_classic.chains import RetrievalQA  # F3
from langchain_core.prompts import ChatPromptTemplate  # F3.1: RAG System Prompt & Persona
from langchain_core.prompts.chat import SystemMessagePromptTemplate, HumanMessagePromptTemplate  # F3.1

from core.llm import build_llm_and_embeddings  # F2/F12
from core.memory import wrap_with_memory  # F7
from core.vectorstore import get_retriever  # F3/F10/F12
from engines.base import BaseMenuEngine  # F12

load_dotenv(find_dotenv())

AVAILABLE_CUISINES = ["sushi", "steak", "italian"]

# F12: same persona/guardrail prompt as menu_api.py's RAG_SYSTEM_PROMPT (F3.1), plus one added
# guideline (retain policy specifics) not yet mirrored back into menu_api.py's copy.
RAG_SYSTEM_PROMPT = """You are a friendly, knowledgeable restaurant assistant. Answer guest questions
using ONLY the menu and restaurant information given in the context below - never
invent dishes, prices, ingredients, allergens, or policies that aren't explicitly
there.

Guidelines:
- If the answer isn't in the provided context, say so plainly (e.g. "I don't have
  that information") rather than guessing.
- If the question references a specific date or day (e.g. "today", "Friday",
  "this weekend"), use that to figure out which part of the context applies.
- Keep answers concise and conversational, like speaking to a guest at the
  restaurant - not a bulleted data dump unless they asked for a list.
- Mention prices when referencing specific dishes, if the context gives them.
- When answering about restaurant policies (hours, parking, payment, reservations,
  dress code, corkage, delivery/takeout), state the specific details given in the
  context (fees, time limits, exceptions) rather than a vague paraphrase.
- If asked about something outside the menu or restaurant policies, politely
  redirect back to what you can help with instead of answering off-topic.
----------------
{context}"""

RAG_PROMPT = ChatPromptTemplate.from_messages([
    SystemMessagePromptTemplate.from_template(RAG_SYSTEM_PROMPT),
    HumanMessagePromptTemplate.from_template("{question}"),
])


class PlainRagEngine(BaseMenuEngine):  # F12: today's RetrievalQA logic, behind the shared interface
    def __init__(self):
        self.llm, self.embeddings = build_llm_and_embeddings()  # F2/F12
        self.qa_chains = {}
        self.qa_chains_with_memory = {}  # F7
        for cuisine in AVAILABLE_CUISINES:
            chain = self._build_qa_chain(cuisine)
            self.qa_chains[cuisine] = chain
            self.qa_chains_with_memory[cuisine] = wrap_with_memory(  # F7
                lambda q, chain=chain: chain.invoke({"query": q})
            )

    def _build_qa_chain(self, cuisine: str):  # F3/F12: same steps as menu_api.py's build_qa_chain()
        retriever = get_retriever(cuisine, self.embeddings)  # F3/F10/F12
        return RetrievalQA.from_chain_type(
            llm=self.llm,
            retriever=retriever,
            return_source_documents=True,
            chain_type_kwargs={"prompt": RAG_PROMPT},
        )

    def answer(self, cuisine: str, question: str, session_id: str, use_memory: bool = True) -> dict:
        if cuisine not in self.qa_chains:
            raise ValueError(f"Unknown cuisine: {cuisine}")
        if not use_memory:  # F8: hours questions bypass memory, same reasoning as menu_api.py
            return self.qa_chains[cuisine].invoke({"query": question})
        memory_config = {"configurable": {"session_id": f"{cuisine}:{session_id}"}}  # F7
        return self.qa_chains_with_memory[cuisine].invoke({"query": question}, config=memory_config)

#!/usr/bin/env python
# coding: utf-8

# F12: Modular Engine Strategy Factory - the new entry point that answers questions through
# BaseMenuEngine/get_engine() instead of building a RetrievalQA chain inline. menu_api.py is
# left untouched on purpose (still runnable standalone) - this file duplicates its ops-intent
# (F8) helpers and routes rather than importing from it.
import os
from dotenv import load_dotenv, find_dotenv
from typing import Optional
from fastapi import FastAPI
from pydantic import BaseModel

from core.telemetry import UsageInfo, new_session_totals, track_usage, new_trace_totals, trace_call, log_trace  # F6, F9
from core.database import init_db, log_call, get_session_totals  # F11
from core.sheets import get_daily_specials, get_hours_and_events, detect_ops_intent, resolve_target_days  # F8
from engines.base import get_engine  # F12

load_dotenv(find_dotenv())

DEBUG_MODE = os.environ.get("DEBUG_MODE", "true").lower() != "false"
DEFAULT_ENGINE = os.environ.get("DEFAULT_ENGINE", "plain_rag")  # F12: which engine answers by default

AVAILABLE_CUISINES = ["sushi", "steak", "italian"]

app = FastAPI()

session_usage_totals = new_session_totals()  # F6
session_trace_totals = new_trace_totals()  # F9
init_db()  # F11: create usage_log table if it doesn't exist yet


class AskRequest(BaseModel):
    cuisine: str
    question: str
    session_id: str = "default"  # F7
    engine: Optional[str] = None  # F12: per-request override of DEFAULT_ENGINE


def format_specials_answer(rows: list[dict]) -> str:  # F8: shared by /ask and the CLI
    if not rows:
        return "There are no active specials for that day."
    lines = [f"[{row['Day']}] {row['Dish Name']} ({row['Price']}) - {row['Description']}" for row in rows]
    return "Specials:\n" + "\n".join(lines)


def format_hours_events(rows: list[dict]) -> str:  # F8: shared by /ask and the CLI - "" when there's nothing to append
    if not rows:
        return ""
    lines = [
        f"{row['Date']} ({row['Day']}) - {row['Event / Holiday']}: {row['Status']} "
        f"{row['Open Time']}-{row['Close Time']}"
        for row in rows
    ]
    return "\n\nGoogle Sheets (F8) - holiday/event schedule for that day:\n" + "\n".join(lines)


def specials_for_question(question: str) -> list[dict]:  # F8: resolves tomorrow/weekend/a weekday/etc., dedupes "All Week" rows
    rows, seen = [], set()
    for d in resolve_target_days(question):
        for row in get_daily_specials(d.strftime("%a")):
            if row["Dish Name"] not in seen:
                seen.add(row["Dish Name"])
                rows.append(row)
    return rows


def hours_for_question(question: str) -> list[dict]:  # F8: resolves tomorrow/weekend/a weekday/etc.
    rows = []
    for d in resolve_target_days(question):
        rows.extend(get_hours_and_events(d.isoformat()))
    return rows


def with_date_context(question: str) -> str:  # F8: shared by /ask and the CLI
    target_days = resolve_target_days(question)
    if len(target_days) == 1:
        d = target_days[0]
        prefix = f"The date being asked about is {d.strftime('%A')}, {d.isoformat()}. "
    else:
        parts = ", ".join(f"{d.strftime('%A')} {d.isoformat()}" for d in target_days)
        prefix = f"The dates being asked about are: {parts}. "
    return prefix + question


@app.post("/ask")
def ask(request: AskRequest):
    cuisine = request.cuisine.strip().lower()
    if cuisine not in AVAILABLE_CUISINES:
        return {"error": f"Unknown cuisine. Choose one of {AVAILABLE_CUISINES}"}

    if request.question.strip().lower() == "tt":  # F11: totals-only shortcut, works regardless of DEBUG_MODE
        return {"cuisine": cuisine, "session_totals": get_session_totals(request.session_id)}

    ops_intent = detect_ops_intent(request.question)  # F8: route obvious specials/hours questions to the live sheet
    if ops_intent == "specials":  # F8: specials only ever live in the sheet, never in the PDF menus - go straight there
        if DEBUG_MODE:
            print("\n[F8] Accessing MCP data source (Google Sheets) - question routed to specials...")
        try:
            answer = format_specials_answer(specials_for_question(request.question))
        except RuntimeError as e:
            return {"error": str(e)}
        return {
            "cuisine": cuisine,
            "answer": answer,
            "top_match": "(F8) Live data from Google Sheets, not a PDF chunk",
        }
    # ops_intent == "hours" is NOT short-circuited here - standard hours might genuinely be in the PDF
    # menu, so the engine gets first crack at it below; only falls back to F8 if it comes up empty.

    # F8: give the engine the resolved date(s) for hours questions (today/tomorrow/a weekday/weekend/etc.),
    # so it can resolve against the PDF's static weekly schedule.
    question_for_engine = with_date_context(request.question) if ops_intent == "hours" else request.question
    use_memory = ops_intent != "hours"  # F8: hours questions bypass Ephemeral Chat Memory (F7), same reasoning as menu_api.py

    engine_name = request.engine or DEFAULT_ENGINE  # F12
    engine = get_engine(engine_name)  # F12

    def invoke_engine():
        return engine.answer(cuisine, question_for_engine, request.session_id, use_memory=use_memory)  # F12

    if DEBUG_MODE:  # F6: only track usage when the toggle is on
        with track_usage(session_usage_totals) as cb, trace_call(session_trace_totals) as timer:  # F9
            result = invoke_engine()
        usage = UsageInfo(
            prompt_tokens=cb.prompt_tokens,
            completion_tokens=cb.completion_tokens,
            total_tokens=cb.total_tokens,
            total_cost_usd=cb.total_cost,
        )
        log_call(cuisine, request.session_id, request.question, usage)  # F11: persist this call
        durable_totals = get_session_totals(request.session_id)  # F11: durable totals from usage_log, not memory
    else:  # F6: toggle off - skip tracking entirely
        result = invoke_engine()
        usage = None
        durable_totals = None
        timer = None

    answer = result["result"]
    top_match = result["source_documents"][0].page_content
    if ops_intent == "hours":  # F8: always append any live-sheet exceptions/events for the resolved date(s)
        if DEBUG_MODE:
            print("\n[F8] Accessing MCP data source (Google Sheets) - appending any events for the resolved date(s)...")
        try:
            answer += format_hours_events(hours_for_question(request.question))
        except RuntimeError:
            pass  # F8 lookup failed - keep the engine's answer as-is, nothing to append

    response = {
        "cuisine": cuisine,
        "answer": answer,
        "top_match": top_match,
        "engine": engine_name,  # F12: which engine answered - useful once F13/F14/F15 exist
    }
    if usage is not None:  # F6: only include usage in the response when the toggle is on
        response["usage"] = usage
        response["session_totals"] = durable_totals  # F11: durable, SQL-backed totals (not the in-memory F6 dict)
    if timer is not None:  # F9: only include the latency/error breakdown when the toggle is on
        response["trace"] = {
            "retriever_ms": round(timer.retriever_ms, 1),
            "llm_ms": round(timer.llm_ms, 1),
            "total_ms": round(timer.total_ms, 1),
            "errors": session_trace_totals["errors"],
            "calls": session_trace_totals["calls"],
        }
    return response


@app.get("/specials")
def specials(day: Optional[str] = None):  # F8: same core.sheets logic api/mcp_server.py exposes as an MCP tool
    try:
        return {"specials": get_daily_specials(day)}
    except RuntimeError as e:
        return {"error": str(e)}


@app.get("/hours")
def hours(date: Optional[str] = None):  # F8: same core.sheets logic api/mcp_server.py exposes as an MCP tool
    try:
        return {"hours": get_hours_and_events(date)}
    except RuntimeError as e:
        return {"error": str(e)}


# Only runs when this file is executed directly (python3 engine_api.py),
# not when uvicorn imports it to serve the API
if __name__ == "__main__":
    cuisine = input(f"Which menu cuisine would you like ({'/'.join(AVAILABLE_CUISINES)})? ").strip().lower()
    while cuisine not in AVAILABLE_CUISINES:
        cuisine = input(f"Please choose one of menu {'/'.join(AVAILABLE_CUISINES)}: ").strip().lower()

    cli_session_id = "cli"
    cli_engine_name = DEFAULT_ENGINE  # F12: CLI always uses the .env default, no per-call override
    cli_engine = get_engine(cli_engine_name)  # F12

    while True:
        user_query = input(f"\nWhat would you like to know about the {cuisine} menu? (q to quit) ")
        if user_query.strip().lower() == "q":
            break
        if user_query.strip().lower() == "tt":  # F11: totals-only shortcut, works regardless of DEBUG_MODE
            print(f"\n[F11] Session Total (DB) - {get_session_totals(cli_session_id)}")
            continue
        ops_intent = detect_ops_intent(user_query)  # F8: route obvious specials/hours questions to the live sheet
        if ops_intent == "specials":  # F8: specials only ever live in the sheet, never in the PDF menus - go straight there
            if DEBUG_MODE:
                print("\n[F8] Accessing MCP data source (Google Sheets) - question routed to specials...")
            try:
                print(format_specials_answer(specials_for_question(user_query)))
            except RuntimeError as e:
                print(f"[F8] Error: {e}")
            continue
        # ops_intent == "hours" is NOT short-circuited here - see the matching note in ask() above.
        query_for_engine = with_date_context(user_query) if ops_intent == "hours" else user_query  # F8
        use_memory = ops_intent != "hours"  # F8

        def invoke_engine():
            return cli_engine.answer(cuisine, query_for_engine, cli_session_id, use_memory=use_memory)  # F12

        if DEBUG_MODE:  # F6: track tokens/cost for each interactive question too
            with track_usage(session_usage_totals) as cb, trace_call(session_trace_totals) as timer:  # F9
                user_result = invoke_engine()
            usage = UsageInfo(
                prompt_tokens=cb.prompt_tokens,
                completion_tokens=cb.completion_tokens,
                total_tokens=cb.total_tokens,
                total_cost_usd=cb.total_cost,
            )
            log_call(cuisine, cli_session_id, user_query, usage)  # F11: persist this call
            print(f"\n[F6] Tokens - prompt: {cb.prompt_tokens}, completion: {cb.completion_tokens}, "
                  f"total: {cb.total_tokens} | Cost: ${cb.total_cost:.6f}")
            print(f"[F11] Session Total (DB) - {get_session_totals(cli_session_id)}")
            log_trace(timer, session_trace_totals)  # F9: retriever/LLM latency + error rate
        else:  # F6: toggle off - skip tracking entirely
            user_result = invoke_engine()

        answer = user_result["result"]
        if ops_intent == "hours":  # F8: always append any live-sheet exceptions/events for the resolved date(s)
            if DEBUG_MODE:
                print("\n[F8] Accessing MCP data source (Google Sheets) - appending any events for the resolved date(s)...")
            try:
                answer += format_hours_events(hours_for_question(user_query))
            except RuntimeError as e:
                print(f"[F8] Error: {e}")
        print("\nAnswer:", answer)

Line-by-Line Deep Dive

base.py L13 _engine_instances singleton cache
A module-level dict, not an instance attribute anywhere — every caller of get_engine("plain_rag") across the whole process gets back the exact same PlainRagEngine, so its per-cuisine FAISS indexes and provider clients are built exactly once, the first time any request or CLI session asks for that engine.
base.py L19 lazy import inside get_engine
from engines.plain_rag_engine import PlainRagEngine happens inside the function body, not at module top level — engines/base.py can be imported on its own without plain_rag_engine.py existing, and it avoids a circular-import risk once LangGraph State Machine Engine (F13)/CrewAI Multi-Role Engine (F14)/AutoGen Multi-Agent Engine (F15) each add their own module that also needs to import from base.py.
plain_rag_engine.py answer() use_memory branch
Directly mirrors FastMCP Server Endpoint (F8)'s reasoning in menu_api.py: hours questions bypass Ephemeral Chat Memory (F7) entirely, because prior conversation turns about menu items were diluting the embedding used for retrieval. Same bypass, reimplemented behind the interface instead of inline in /ask.
engine_api.py DEFAULT_ENGINE / AskRequest.engine
Two independent knobs, matching the pattern DEBUG_MODE already established: an .env default for normal operation, plus a per-request override for testing a specific engine without restarting the server or editing .env. Deliberately not reusing DEBUG_MODE itself for this — that variable controls print-statement verbosity, an unrelated concern.
The shared-session retrieval gotcha (found while testing F12.1)
Neither gradio_app.py nor streamlit_app.py sends a session_id to /ask, so every UI session (and every curl test) lands in the same "default" Ephemeral Chat Memory (F7) bucket. Once that bucket accumulates enough prior turns, short/ambiguous queries like "parking" or "policies" get their embedding diluted by unrelated conversation history and retrieval starts missing chunks it found correctly on a fresh session — confirmed directly: the same question answered correctly on a brand-new session_id and failed on the well-used "default" one. Not a bug introduced by F12/F12.1 — it's the same dilution mechanism the F8 hours-bypass-memory branch already works around, just previously unnoticed because nothing had exercised a long-lived shared session against a short keyword query before.
Interview angle — "Why a separate engine_api.py instead of just editing menu_api.py's /ask in place?" This is a deliberate strangler-fig-style migration, not indecision: menu_api.py is kept as a stable, always-working reference implementation throughout the multi-engine rollout (LangGraph State Machine Engine F13, CrewAI Multi-Role Engine F14, AutoGen Multi-Agent Engine F15), so there's never a point where the whole app is mid-refactor and nothing runs cleanly. The honest cost is real, though: F8's helper functions and routes now have two copies to keep in sync by hand, and that duplication only grows if more shared logic gets added to menu_api.py later without a matching update to engine_api.py. The trade a production team would actually make here is time-boxed — treat engine_api.py as the eventual replacement, delete menu_api.py once LangGraph State Machine Engine (F13) is stable, rather than running both indefinitely.

F13:1 LangGraph State Machine Engine: From One Fixed Answer to a Graph That Can Check Itself

Every engine behind Modular Engine Strategy Factory (F12) until now has run the same three unconditional steps: retrieve, generate, done. That's fine when retrieval hands back the right chunks and the model's first answer is grounded in them — but there's no step that ever asks "was it?" A question that FAISS retrieves poorly for, or a model that quietly invents a detail not in the context, gets the same one-shot treatment as a question that went perfectly. There's also no step that filters an off-topic question before spending a retrieval and a generation call on it — that's still handled by menu_api.py/engine_api.py's own detect_ops_intent keyword check, outside any engine.

LangGraph State Machine Engine turns that fixed sequence into a small graph with a decision at two points instead of zero: a routing node up front that can reject an off-topic question before any retrieval happens, and a verify node at the end that grades whether the answer is actually grounded in what was retrieved — looping back to retrieve again, with the rejection reason folded into the next attempt, if it isn't. It's the same contract as Modular Engine Strategy Factory (F12)'s PlainRagEngine — same answer() signature, same return shape — so engine_api.py and everything upstream of it don't know or care that a graph is running instead of a single chain.

The Big Picture: How the Graph Is Structured

Five nodes, wired with two conditional edges:

  • route (_route_node): a structured LLM call (RouteDecision) classifying the question as on-topic or off-topic — a more principled version of FastMCP Server Endpoint (F8)'s keyword-based detect_ops_intent, run per-question inside the engine instead of ahead of it
  • retrieve (_retrieve_node): the exact same core/vectorstore.py retriever Modular Engine Strategy Factory (F12) uses (FAISS + Cross-Encoder Re-ranking (F10)) — no new retrieval logic, just a new place to call it from, including a second time on a retry
  • generate (_generate_node): an LLM call against the same RAG_PROMPT persona as PlainRagEngine; on a retry, the verifier's rejection reason gets appended to the question so the second attempt has something concrete to fix, instead of just asking the same thing again
  • verify (_verify_node): a second structured LLM call (VerifyDecision) grading whether the generated answer is actually supported by the retrieved context — the "good enough" vs. "try again" decision, bounded by MAX_RETRIES = 2 total attempts so a stubbornly ungrounded answer can't loop forever
  • redirect (_redirect_node): a canned response for the off-topic branch — no retrieval or generation call spent on a question the graph already knows it can't (or shouldn't) answer

What's Imported (and Why)

  • langgraph.graph.StateGraph, END — the graph itself: add_node/add_edge/add_conditional_edges wire the five nodes above, and .compile() turns the wiring into something with a .invoke() method, just like the RetrievalQA chain it replaces.
  • TypedDict (Python standard library) — GraphState's shape; LangGraph threads this dict through every node, merging each node's returned partial dict into it.
  • pydantic.BaseModel — RouteDecision/VerifyDecision, passed to llm.with_structured_output(...) so the route/verify nodes get a typed boolean back instead of parsing free text out of a chat response.
  • core.llm.build_llm_and_embeddings, core.vectorstore.get_retriever, core.memory.wrap_with_memory — the same three shared helpers PlainRagEngine uses (see Modular Engine Strategy Factory (F12)'s "Where the Shared Helpers Plug In") — nothing new imported for provider setup, retrieval, or memory; only the graph-specific pieces above are new.

For the full, step-by-step code implementation, class structures, and technical configuration, please refer to the GitHub Repository & Code Details link.

Tags: Graph Engineering, Loop Engineering, Agentic AI, F13

Tools & Libraries (per checklist.csv's "Primary Tools & Libraries" for #13):
  • StateGraph / Conditional Edges — used. Five nodes, two conditional edges (route's on-topic/off-topic branch and verify's retry/done branch) — exactly the checklist's named tool, no heavier agent framework needed for a graph this small.
  • Structured output (with_structured_output) — used, not called out in the checklist by name, but it's what makes the route/verify decisions typed booleans instead of regex-parsed text — the same reliability upgrade over keyword-matching that FastMCP Server Endpoint (F8)'s detect_ops_intent could eventually get from Query Guardrails & Intent Gating (F19).

Module: engines/langgraph_engine.py (new file) — matches checklist.csv's Target Location for #13.

Class: GraphState(TypedDict) — the state threaded through every node: cuisine, question, on_topic, documents, answer, grounded, verify_feedback, and attempts (the retry counter _after_verify checks against MAX_RETRIES).

Classes: RouteDecision / VerifyDecision (BaseModel) — RouteDecision is just on_topic: bool; VerifyDecision is grounded: bool plus a reasoning: str that _generate_node reads back on a retry, so the model sees why its last answer was rejected, not just that it was.

Class: LangGraphEngine(BaseMenuEngine) — on construction, builds provider clients via core.llm.build_llm_and_embeddings() and one retriever per cuisine via core.vectorstore.get_retriever() (identical to PlainRagEngine), then compiles one graph per cuisine and wraps it in core.memory.wrap_with_memory(...). answer(...) has the exact same use_memory branch as PlainRagEngine.answer() — hours questions bypass memory and call the graph directly, everything else goes through the memory wrapper first.

Request Trace: Agentic Flow (F13)

How one POST /ask call with engine: "langgraph" actually flows — reusing Modular Engine Strategy Factory (F12)'s shared helpers rather than duplicating them a third time (see F12's "Where the Shared Helpers Plug In" above):

  • engine_api.py — same entry as the non-agentic path, up through get_engine("langgraph")
    • lazily imports engines/langgraph_engine.py, instantiates LangGraphEngine(), caches it
  • engines/langgraph_engine.py — LangGraphEngine.__init__() (once per process)
    • core/llm.py: build_llm_and_embeddings() — identical call to the non-agentic path
    • per cuisine, core/vectorstore.py: get_retriever(cuisine, embeddings) — same shared retriever, no duplicate FAISS pipeline
    • _build_graph() — wires a StateGraph: route → (retrieve | redirect), retrieve → generate → verify, verify → (retrieve again | done), compiled once per cuisine
    • core/memory.py: wrap_with_memory(...) — same memory wrapping as F12, around the whole graph invocation
  • engines/langgraph_engine.py — LangGraphEngine.answer(...)
    • use_memory=False (hours questions) → invokes the compiled graph directly, same branch F12 uses
    • use_memory=True → through core/memory.py's wrapper first, exactly like PlainRagEngine.answer(...)
    • either way, running the compiled graph means:
      • _route_node — a structured LLM call (RouteDecision) classifying on-topic vs. off-topic — the "more principled" replacement for F8's detect_ops_intent the checklist calls for
      • off-topic → _redirect_node — canned redirect, no retrieval or generation spent → graph ends
      • on-topic → _retrieve_node — the same core/vectorstore.py retriever as F12 (FAISS + F10's cross-encoder re-ranking)
      • _generate_node — an LLM call against RAG_PROMPT plus the retrieved context; on a retry, folds the verifier's rejection reason into the question so the second attempt has something concrete to fix
      • _verify_node — a second structured LLM call (VerifyDecision) grading whether the answer is actually grounded in the retrieved context
        • grounded, or attempts has reached MAX_RETRIES → graph ends
        • not grounded and retries remain → loops back to _retrieve_node — the bounded self-correction loop
    • returns {"result": ..., "source_documents": ...} — the same shape PlainRagEngine.answer() returns, so nothing downstream needs to know which engine answered
  • back in engine_api.py — identical to the non-agentic path from here: core/telemetry.py usage/latency tracking, core/database.py call logging, an hours-append via core/sheets.py if needed, then the final JSON response (now with "engine": "langgraph")

The only genuinely new file in this path versus the non-agentic one is engines/langgraph_engine.py itself and the graph nodes inside it — everything upstream (engine_api.py) and every piece of shared infrastructure downstream (core/llm.py, core/vectorstore.py, core/memory.py, core/telemetry.py, core/database.py, core/sheets.py) is exactly the same code the non-agentic path already runs. That reuse is what Modular Engine Strategy Factory (F12) actually buys: a new answering strategy becomes one new engine file, not a rewrite of the request pipeline around it.

Verification: the retry loop, off-topic redirect, and bounded termination were each tested standalone with a fake LLM/retriever (no API cost) before running the real thing — a fake verifier that always returns grounded=False confirms the graph stops after exactly MAX_RETRIES generate attempts instead of looping forever. Then verified live: a real on-topic question through get_engine("langgraph").answer(...) (route → retrieve → generate → verify, grounded on the first attempt, 4 total API calls), a real off-topic question (route → redirect, 1 API call, no retrieval/generation spent), and a full HTTP round trip through engine_api.py's /ask with {"engine": "langgraph"} — F6/F9's usage and latency tracking worked with zero changes, since they wrap invoke_engine() generically regardless of which engine answered.

The off-topic HTTP test caught a real bug this way: engine_api.py's /ask unconditionally read result["source_documents"][0] for top_match — safe for every engine so far, since PlainRagEngine's FAISS retriever always returns at least one chunk even for a nonsense question, but LangGraphEngine's _redirect_node legitimately returns an empty list, which crashed the endpoint with an IndexError before any response was sent. Fixed with a one-line guard (engine_api.py:140): top_match = result["source_documents"][0].page_content if result["source_documents"] else "".

F13:4 Testing Guide: How to test LangGraph State Machine Engine (F13)

Setup — install the new dependency (already added to requirements.txt):

source venv/bin/activate
pip install langgraph

1) CLI, as the default engine — the CLI always uses DEFAULT_ENGINE, with no per-call override (same limitation as Modular Engine Strategy Factory (F12.1)'s CLI). If DEBUG_MODE is on, the interactive prompt lets you pick 2) LangGraph for one run without touching .env at all — otherwise, add one line to the repo-root .env (same file as OPENAI_API_KEY):

DEFAULT_ENGINE=langgraph
source venv/bin/activate
python3 engine_api.py

Pick a cuisine (and, in DEBUG_MODE, engine 2) and ask a question — the CLI now answers through the graph instead of PlainRagEngine's single chain. Remove the .env line (or set it back to DEFAULT_ENGINE=plain_rag) to switch back permanently.

2) FastAPI — curl, Postman, or the Gradio/Streamlit UIs, same as Modular Engine Strategy Factory (F12)/F12.1's testing above; start the server once:

uvicorn engine_api:app --reload --port 8000

curl — per-request engine override, no server restart or config change needed, same mechanism as any other engine name:

curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/ask -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"cuisine": "sushi", "question": "What rolls do you have?", "engine": "langgraph"}'

The response includes "engine": "langgraph", plus the usual F6 usage/F9 trace objects — proving the graph ran end to end and that both wrap generically over whichever engine answered. See the routing node reject an off-topic question with the same endpoint:

curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/ask -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"cuisine": "sushi", "question": "What is the weather like today?", "engine": "langgraph"}'

The answer comes back as the canned redirect ("I'm not able to help with that..."), and — unlike an on-topic question — top_match is empty and only one LLM call was made, since the graph's route node short-circuits straight to redirect without ever reaching retrieve/generate.

Postman — same two requests as above: method POST, URL http://127.0.0.1:8000/ask, Content-Type: application/json header, each JSON body pasted in raw.

Gradio / Streamlit — same as F12/F12.1: neither UI exposes an engine selector, so both only exercise DEFAULT_ENGINE. Set DEFAULT_ENGINE=langgraph in the repo-root .env first if you want to see the graph answer through the UI layer, same as step 1's CLI setup above.

Seeing the self-correction loop actually trigger: in normal use, gpt-4o-mini usually gets a small, well-scoped menu question right on the first attempt (as in step 2's curl example above), so _verify_node rarely rejects it and the retry branch rarely fires against the real menus. The retry loop itself is exercised deterministically with a scripted fake LLM/retriever instead (see the Verification note above) — that's the reliable way to see _after_verify's "retry" branch and the bounded-termination behavior without depending on the model happening to produce an ungrounded answer.

# F13: LangGraph State Machine Engine - upgrades the single fixed retrieve+generate step
# (Modular Engine Strategy Factory (F12)'s PlainRagEngine) into a graph that routes,
# retries, and self-corrects. A second engine behind BaseMenuEngine, selectable the same
# way as plain_rag (engines/base.py's get_engine()). Duplicates rather than extracts
# shared setup from plain_rag_engine.py, same reasoning as F12.1 - core.llm/core.vectorstore
# are shared (F12), the RAG chain/persona and graph wiring below are this engine's own.
from typing import TypedDict

from dotenv import load_dotenv, find_dotenv
from langchain_core.documents import Document
from langchain_core.prompts import ChatPromptTemplate  # F3.1
from langchain_core.prompts.chat import SystemMessagePromptTemplate, HumanMessagePromptTemplate  # F3.1
from langgraph.graph import StateGraph, END  # F13
from pydantic import BaseModel  # F13: structured route/verify output

from core.llm import build_llm_and_embeddings  # F2/F12
from core.memory import wrap_with_memory  # F7
from core.vectorstore import get_retriever  # F3/F10/F12
from engines.base import BaseMenuEngine  # F12

load_dotenv(find_dotenv())

AVAILABLE_CUISINES = ["sushi", "steak", "italian"]
MAX_RETRIES = 2  # F13: bounded retry loop - self-correct at most this many times, then give up

# F13: same persona/guardrail prompt as plain_rag_engine.py's RAG_SYSTEM_PROMPT (F3.1/F12)
RAG_SYSTEM_PROMPT = """You are a friendly, knowledgeable restaurant assistant. Answer guest questions
using ONLY the menu and restaurant information given in the context below - never
invent dishes, prices, ingredients, allergens, or policies that aren't explicitly
there.

Guidelines:
- If the answer isn't in the provided context, say so plainly (e.g. "I don't have
  that information") rather than guessing.
- If the question references a specific date or day (e.g. "today", "Friday",
  "this weekend"), use that to figure out which part of the context applies.
- Keep answers concise and conversational, like speaking to a guest at the
  restaurant - not a bulleted data dump unless they asked for a list.
- Mention prices when referencing specific dishes, if the context gives them.
- When answering about restaurant policies (hours, parking, payment, reservations,
  dress code, corkage, delivery/takeout), state the specific details given in the
  context (fees, time limits, exceptions) rather than a vague paraphrase.
----------------
{context}"""

RAG_PROMPT = ChatPromptTemplate.from_messages([
    SystemMessagePromptTemplate.from_template(RAG_SYSTEM_PROMPT),
    HumanMessagePromptTemplate.from_template("{question}"),
])


class RouteDecision(BaseModel):  # F13: routing node's structured output
    on_topic: bool


class VerifyDecision(BaseModel):  # F13: verify node's structured output
    grounded: bool
    reasoning: str


class GraphState(TypedDict):  # F13: state threaded through every node in the graph
    cuisine: str
    question: str
    on_topic: bool
    documents: list[Document]
    answer: str
    grounded: bool
    verify_feedback: str
    attempts: int


class LangGraphEngine(BaseMenuEngine):  # F13: retrieve/generate/verify as a graph, behind F12's interface
    def __init__(self):
        self.llm, self.embeddings = build_llm_and_embeddings()  # F2/F12
        self.retrievers = {}
        self.graphs = {}
        self.chains_with_memory = {}  # F7
        for cuisine in AVAILABLE_CUISINES:
            self.retrievers[cuisine] = get_retriever(cuisine, self.embeddings)  # F3/F10/F12
            self.graphs[cuisine] = self._build_graph()
            self.chains_with_memory[cuisine] = wrap_with_memory(  # F7
                lambda q, cuisine=cuisine: self._invoke_graph(cuisine, q)
            )

    # ---- graph nodes ----

    def _route_node(self, state: GraphState) -> dict:  # F13: principled replacement for F8's detect_ops_intent
        router = self.llm.with_structured_output(RouteDecision)
        decision = router.invoke(
            "Is this question about a restaurant's menu, dishes, hours, or policies? "
            f"Question: {state['question']}"
        )
        return {"on_topic": decision.on_topic}

    def _retrieve_node(self, state: GraphState) -> dict:
        documents = self.retrievers[state["cuisine"]].invoke(state["question"])
        return {"documents": documents}

    def _generate_node(self, state: GraphState) -> dict:
        context = "\n\n".join(doc.page_content for doc in state["documents"])
        question = state["question"]
        if state["attempts"] > 0 and state["verify_feedback"]:  # F13: fold verifier feedback into the retry
            question = (
                f"{question}\n\n(Your previous answer was rejected: {state['verify_feedback']}. "
                "Try again, using only the context below.)"
            )
        messages = RAG_PROMPT.format_messages(context=context, question=question)
        response = self.llm.invoke(messages)
        return {"answer": response.content}

    def _verify_node(self, state: GraphState) -> dict:  # F13: "good enough" vs "try again"
        context = "\n\n".join(doc.page_content for doc in state["documents"])
        verifier = self.llm.with_structured_output(VerifyDecision)
        decision = verifier.invoke(
            f"Context:\n{context}\n\nQuestion: {state['question']}\n\nAnswer: {state['answer']}\n\n"
            "Is the answer fully supported by the context, with nothing invented?"
        )
        return {
            "grounded": decision.grounded,
            "verify_feedback": decision.reasoning,
            "attempts": state["attempts"] + 1,
        }

    def _redirect_node(self, state: GraphState) -> dict:  # F13: off-topic branch, no retrieval/LLM call spent
        return {
            "answer": "I'm not able to help with that - I can answer questions about our menu, hours, and policies.",
            "documents": [],
        }

    # ---- conditional edges ----

    def _after_route(self, state: GraphState) -> str:
        return "on_topic" if state["on_topic"] else "off_topic"

    def _after_verify(self, state: GraphState) -> str:  # F13: bounded retry loop
        if state["grounded"] or state["attempts"] >= MAX_RETRIES:
            return "done"
        return "retry"

    def _build_graph(self):
        graph = StateGraph(GraphState)
        graph.add_node("route", self._route_node)
        graph.add_node("retrieve", self._retrieve_node)
        graph.add_node("generate", self._generate_node)
        graph.add_node("verify", self._verify_node)
        graph.add_node("redirect", self._redirect_node)

        graph.set_entry_point("route")
        graph.add_conditional_edges("route", self._after_route, {"on_topic": "retrieve", "off_topic": "redirect"})
        graph.add_edge("retrieve", "generate")
        graph.add_edge("generate", "verify")
        graph.add_conditional_edges("verify", self._after_verify, {"retry": "retrieve", "done": END})
        graph.add_edge("redirect", END)
        return graph.compile()

    def _invoke_graph(self, cuisine: str, question: str) -> dict:
        result = self.graphs[cuisine].invoke({
            "cuisine": cuisine,
            "question": question,
            "on_topic": True,
            "documents": [],
            "answer": "",
            "grounded": False,
            "verify_feedback": "",
            "attempts": 0,
        })
        return {"result": result["answer"], "source_documents": result["documents"]}

    def answer(self, cuisine: str, question: str, session_id: str, use_memory: bool = True) -> dict:
        if cuisine not in self.graphs:
            raise ValueError(f"Unknown cuisine: {cuisine}")
        if not use_memory:  # F8: hours questions bypass memory, same reasoning as plain_rag_engine.py
            return self._invoke_graph(cuisine, question)
        memory_config = {"configurable": {"session_id": f"{cuisine}:{session_id}"}}  # F7
        return self.chains_with_memory[cuisine].invoke({"query": question}, config=memory_config)

F16 — Persistent Thread Checkpointing

Jump to: F16:1 Persistent Thread Checkpointing · F16:2 Architecture Summary · F16:3 Integration Guide (core/memory.py) · F16:4 Testing Guide · F16:5 Source Code Reference (core/memory.py) · F16:6 Source Code Reference: TBA · F16:7 Line-by-Line Deep Dive · F16:8 Technical Deep Dive

Status: Implemented. Ephemeral Chat Memory (F7) stored each session's chat history in a module-level Python dict — fast, but wiped the instant the server restarts or crashes. F16 adds a second, durable backend for that same history, selected via a MEMORY_BACKEND env var, so a conversation survives a restart instead of vanishing with it.

Maps to checklist.csv day 16, "Persistent Thread Checkpointing." The checklist's original target location was engines/langgraph_engine.py via LangGraph's SqliteSaver — the actual implementation below targets F7's own module, core/memory.py, instead. See F16:8 for why.

↑ Back to F16

F16:1 Persistent Thread Checkpointing: Why a Restart Shouldn't Erase the Conversation

Ephemeral Chat Memory (F7) already solved the "goldfish memory" problem within a single process — the assistant remembers what a customer said five minutes ago, as long as the server that answered them is still the one running. The moment that process restarts (a deploy, a crash, a routine redeploy), F7's _session_histories dict is gone. Every open conversation reverts to a stranger, mid-sentence.

F16 doesn't replace F7's memory logic — the sliding window, the context-injection format, the RunnableWithMessageHistory wiring all stay exactly as they were. It replaces where the messages live: instead of a Python dict that only exists inside one running process, a session's history can now be written to a SQLite file on disk. Kill the process, start it again, send a follow-up with the same session_id, and the assistant still has the earlier turns — because they were never only in RAM to begin with.

The Big Picture: One Function, Two Backends

Everything upstream of memory storage — menu_api.py, both engines, F7's sliding window and prompt-injection format — calls exactly one function, get_session_history(session_id), and only ever sees its return type, BaseChatMessageHistory. F16 adds a second branch inside that one function: MEMORY_BACKEND=ephemeral (default) returns F7's original in-memory ChatMessageHistory; MEMORY_BACKEND=persistent returns a SQLChatMessageHistory pointed at a SQLite file instead. Callers never branch on which backend is active — the toggle lives in exactly one place, so nothing downstream had to change to gain durability. See F16:2 for how that stays true even for the history-trimming logic that used to assume an in-memory list.

What's Imported (and Why)

  • SQLChatMessageHistory (from langchain_community.chat_message_histories, the same module F7's ChatMessageHistory already came from) — a drop-in BaseChatMessageHistory implementation backed by SQL instead of RAM, so no new interface had to be hand-rolled to keep wrap_with_memory()'s callers unaware anything changed.
  • sqlalchemy (added explicitly to requirements.txt) — SQLChatMessageHistory's actual storage engine underneath; it was already present transitively via langchain-community, now pinned directly since F16 depends on it by name.
  • os (Python standard library) — reads MEMORY_BACKEND the same way DEBUG_MODE and every other feature flag in this app is read, defaulting to "ephemeral" so an unset or unrecognized value fails safe instead of raising.

For the full, step-by-step code implementation, class structures, and technical configuration, please refer to the GitHub Repository & Code Details link.

Tags: Memory, Persistence, SQLite, F16, F7

F16:2 Architecture Summary: A Toggle, Not a Rewrite

The whole feature is one branch inside core/memory.py's get_session_history() — the single function every other piece of the memory system already calls through. Three moving parts:

  • The backend switch (MEMORY_BACKEND env var): "ephemeral" (default) keeps F7's original in-memory dict; "persistent" switches to a SQLite-backed store. An unrecognized value fails safe to "ephemeral" rather than raising.
  • The persistent store (SQLChatMessageHistory, from the same langchain_community.chat_message_histories module F7's ChatMessageHistory already came from): implements the identical BaseChatMessageHistory interface, so nothing that calls get_session_history() can tell the difference.
  • Trim-on-render (moved from get_session_history() into _render_history()): F7 used to trim the stored history down to MAX_HISTORY_TURNS by mutating .messages in place — a pattern that doesn't work against a SQL-backed history with no such setter. F16 trims what gets rendered into the prompt instead, right before formatting. The full conversation is always kept in storage (RAM or disk); only the window sent to the LLM is bounded.

F16:3 Integration Guide: Integration into core/memory.py

Every caller of F7's memory system — menu_api.py, engines/plain_rag_engine.py, engines/langgraph_engine.py — goes through wrap_with_memory(), never get_session_history() or the storage objects directly. wrap_with_memory()'s signature and return type (RunnableWithMessageHistory) don't change, so F16 required editing exactly one file:

  • core/memory.py — the only file touched. Everything else (menu_api.py, engine_api.py, both engines) is unmodified.
  • requirements.txt — added sqlalchemy explicitly (it was already present transitively via langchain-community, now pinned directly).
  • .gitignore — added chat_history.db, alongside the existing usage.db entry from Relational DB & Text-to-SQL Tool (F11).
  • .env — added MEMORY_BACKEND=ephemeral, alongside DEBUG_MODE and METRICS.

F16:4 Testing Guide: How to test Persistent Thread Checkpointing (F16)

1) Confirm the default (ephemeral) is unchanged — leave MEMORY_BACKEND unset (or ephemeral) in .env, run the app, and confirm multi-turn memory behaves exactly as it did under F7 alone.

2) Prove persistence survives a restart — the actual acceptance test for this feature:

# .env: MEMORY_BACKEND=persistent
uvicorn engine_api:app --reload
# ask a question with a session_id, then a follow-up that depends on it - confirm memory works
# kill the process (not a graceful shutdown - simulate a crash)
uvicorn engine_api:app --reload
# send another follow-up with the SAME session_id
# expect: the assistant still has context from before the restart

3) Inspect the store directly — confirms the rows are actually on disk, not just working by coincidence:

sqlite3 chat_history.db "select session_id, message from message_store;"

4) Confirm the fail-safe default — set MEMORY_BACKEND=nonsense and confirm the app falls back to ephemeral behavior instead of crashing.

F16:5 Source Code Reference: core/memory.py — full file

core/memory.pyF7's ephemeral memory + F16's persistent backend, behind one MEMORY_BACKEND toggle — 71 lines
  1  """F7: Ephemeral in-memory chat history per session, using RunnableWithMessageHistory.
  2  F16: adds a persistent, SQLite-backed alternative via MEMORY_BACKEND, so a session's
  3  history can survive a server restart instead of living only in RAM.
  4  
  5  MEMORY_BACKEND=ephemeral (default) - histories live in a module-level dict, never
  6  touch disk, and reset whenever the process restarts.
  7  MEMORY_BACKEND=persistent - histories are written to a SQLite file (CHAT_HISTORY_DB_PATH)
  8  via SQLChatMessageHistory, surviving a restart or crash.
  9  
 10  Either way, each session's history is trimmed to the last MAX_HISTORY_TURNS exchanges
 11  right before it's rendered into the prompt, to bound context-window token overhead -
 12  the stored history itself is never truncated, only what gets sent to the LLM.
 13  """
 14  import os
 15  
 16  from langchain_community.chat_message_histories import ChatMessageHistory, SQLChatMessageHistory
 17  from langchain_core.chat_history import BaseChatMessageHistory
 18  from langchain_core.runnables import RunnableLambda
 19  from langchain_core.runnables.history import RunnableWithMessageHistory
 20  
 21  DEBUG_MODE = os.environ.get("DEBUG_MODE", "true").lower() != "false"
 22  MEMORY_BACKEND = os.environ.get("MEMORY_BACKEND", "ephemeral").lower()  # F16: "ephemeral" (F7, RAM) or "persistent" (F16, SQLite)
 23  CHAT_HISTORY_DB_PATH = "chat_history.db"  # F16: only used when MEMORY_BACKEND=persistent
 24  
 25  MAX_HISTORY_TURNS = 5  # working context window - keep only the last N exchanges
 26  
 27  _session_histories: dict[str, ChatMessageHistory] = {}  # F7: ephemeral, in-memory, resets on restart
 28  
 29  
 30  def get_session_history(session_id: str) -> BaseChatMessageHistory:
 31      if MEMORY_BACKEND == "persistent":  # F16: durable, survives a restart/crash
 32          return SQLChatMessageHistory(session_id=session_id, connection=f"sqlite:///{CHAT_HISTORY_DB_PATH}")
 33      if session_id not in _session_histories:  # F7: ephemeral (default) - in-memory, resets on restart
 34          _session_histories[session_id] = ChatMessageHistory()
 35      return _session_histories[session_id]
 36  
 37  
 38  def _render_history(messages: list) -> str:
 39      if not messages:
 40          return ""
 41      trimmed = messages[-MAX_HISTORY_TURNS * 2:]  # F16: trim on render, not on storage - full history stays intact either way
 42      lines = [f"{'User' if m.type == 'human' else 'Assistant'}: {m.content}" for m in trimmed]
 43      return "Previous conversation:\n" + "\n".join(lines) + "\n\n"
 44  
 45  
 46  def wrap_with_memory(ask_fn) -> RunnableWithMessageHistory:
 47      """Wrap ask_fn (question: str -> {"result": ..., "source_documents": ...})
 48      so multi-turn context is prepended to the question automatically, and each
 49      exchange is recorded into that session's history afterward.
 50  
 51      Usage:
 52          chain = wrap_with_memory(lambda q: qa_chain.invoke({"query": q}))
 53          chain.invoke({"query": "..."}, config={"configurable": {"session_id": "sushi:default"}})
 54      """
 55  
 56      def _invoke(input: dict, config: dict) -> dict:
 57          history_context = _render_history(input.get("history", []))
 58          contextualized_query = history_context + input["query"]
 59          if DEBUG_MODE and history_context:  # F7: show what memory injected, only when there's something to show
 60              print(f"\n[F7] Contextualized query sent to the chain:\n{contextualized_query}")
 61          return ask_fn(contextualized_query)
 62  
 63      runnable = RunnableLambda(_invoke)
 64      return RunnableWithMessageHistory(
 65          runnable,
 66          get_session_history,
 67          input_messages_key="query",
 68          history_messages_key="history",
 69          output_messages_key="result",
 70      )

F16:7 Line-by-Line Deep Dive: What Changed in core/memory.py

  • Lines 21–23 — two new module-level reads: MEMORY_BACKEND (defaults to "ephemeral", so existing deployments behave identically unless the env var is explicitly set) and CHAT_HISTORY_DB_PATH, the SQLite file's location.
  • Lines 30–35 — get_session_history() now branches first on MEMORY_BACKEND. The "persistent" branch returns a fresh SQLChatMessageHistory pointed at chat_history.db on every call — there's no in-memory caching to go stale, since SQLAlchemy handles the connection underneath. The fallthrough path is F7's original dict logic, untouched.
  • Lines 38–43 — _render_history() gained the trim step that used to live in get_session_history(). Slicing messages[-MAX_HISTORY_TURNS * 2:] here (rather than mutating the stored list) means both backends can share one trimming rule without either needing a .messages setter.
  • Everything below _render_history() — wrap_with_memory() and its inner _invoke() — is byte-for-byte what F7 shipped. It calls get_session_history() the same way regardless of which backend answers.

F16:8 Technical Deep Dive: SQLChatMessageHistory vs. LangGraph's SqliteSaver

The checklist's original plan (engines/langgraph_engine.py, SqliteSaver) targets a different persistence primitive than what F16 actually needed. SqliteSaver checkpoints a compiled StateGraph's internal state — LangGraph State Machine Engine (F13)'s GraphState (attempts, verify_feedback, etc.) — so a graph run can be paused and resumed later. It's built for resuming an interrupted run, not for storing a chat transcript, and wiring it in would have meant threading a thread_id through answer() → _invoke_graph() → graph.compile(checkpointer=...) in F13's engine specifically — helping only that one engine, not plain_rag_engine.py too.

Ephemeral Chat Memory (F7) was already built on BaseChatMessageHistory, an interface designed to be swapped for a persistent implementation — that's the whole reason SQLChatMessageHistory exists as a drop-in alternative to ChatMessageHistory in the same LangChain module. Targeting core/memory.py instead of engines/langgraph_engine.py meant one function changed instead of one engine's internals, and every engine that calls wrap_with_memory() got durable memory for free, not just F13's.

The tradeoff: F16 as built does not checkpoint the LangGraph engine's own mid-run state (a retry loop interrupted mid-attempt still restarts from scratch). It only makes the conversation durable. If resuming an in-flight self-correction loop across a crash ever becomes a real requirement, that's a genuinely separate piece of work — SqliteSaver wired into F13's graph.compile() specifically — layered on top of, not instead of, what F16 built here.

Tags: Memory, Persistence, SQLite, LangGraph, F16, F7, F13

What was built:

  • a MEMORY_BACKEND env var toggle (ephemeral default / persistent) in core/memory.py
  • SQLChatMessageHistory as the persistent backend — same BaseChatMessageHistory interface F7 already used
  • trimming moved from storage-time to render-time, so it works identically for both backends
  • zero changes to any caller — menu_api.py, engine_api.py, both engines — since wrap_with_memory()'s contract is unchanged
